title.zh: 卷二四 列傳第十六 孫搴 陳元康 杜弼
title.en: Volume 24 Biographies 16: Sun Qian (Eastern Wei); Chen Yuankang; Du Bi
title.raw: 卷二四 列傳第十六 孫搴 陳元康 杜弼 Volume 24 Biographies 16: Sun Qian (Eastern Wei); Chen Yuankang; Du Bi

sentences.zh: 孫搴 陳元康 杜弼

translations.literal: Sun Cen; Chen Yuankang; Du Bi
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cen; Chen Yuankang; Du Bi

sentences.zh: 孫搴，字彥舉，樂安人也。

translations.literal: Sun Cen, styled Yanju, was a native of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Cen, styled Yanju, came from Le'an.

sentences.zh: 少厲志勤學，自檢校御史再遷國子助教。

translations.literal: In youth he steeled his will and studied diligently; from investigating censor he was promoted again to assistant instructor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he disciplined himself in study. From investigating censor he rose to assistant instructor at the National University.

sentences.zh: 太保崔光引修國史，頻歷行臺郎，以文才著稱。

translations.literal: Grand Guardian Cui Guang had him compile the national history; he frequently served as mobile headquarters gentleman and was famed for literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Guardian Cui Guang put him to work on the national history. He served repeatedly as mobile headquarters gentleman and won renown for his writing.

sentences.zh: 崔祖螭反，搴預焉，逃於王元景家，遇赦乃出。

translations.literal: When Cui Zuchidi rebelled, Cen was involved; he fled to Wang Yuanjing's house and came out only when amnesty was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Zuchidi rose in rebellion, Cen had been implicated. He hid in Wang Yuanjing's home and emerged only after an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 孫騰以宗情薦之，未被知也。

translations.literal: Sun Teng recommended him on grounds of kinship, but he was not recognized.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Teng recommended him as a clansman, yet he went unnoticed.

sentences.zh: 會高祖西討，登風陵，命中外府司馬李義深、相府城局李士略共作檄文，二人皆辭，請以搴自代。

translations.literal: It happened that the Grand Ancestor campaigned west and ascended Fengling; he ordered Li Yishen, director of the central and outer offices, and Li Shilue of the headquarters city bureau jointly to draft a proclamation — both declined and asked that Cen replace them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan marched west and climbed Fengling, he ordered Li Yishen of the central and outer offices and Li Shilue of the headquarters city bureau to draft a proclamation together. Both declined and asked that Cen take their place.

sentences.zh: 高祖引搴入帳，自為吹火，催促之。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor brought Cen into the tent, himself blew the fire, and urged him on.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan brought Cen into the tent, blew the fire himself, and urged him to write.

sentences.zh: 搴援筆立成，其文甚美。

translations.literal: Cen took the brush and finished at once; the text was very fine.
translations.idiomatic: Cen took up the brush and finished on the spot; the prose was excellent.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，即署相府主簿，專典文筆。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor was greatly pleased and at once appointed him chief clerk of the headquarters, in sole charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan was delighted and immediately made him chief clerk of the headquarters, put exclusively in charge of correspondence.

sentences.zh: 又能通鮮卑語，兼宣傳號令。

translations.literal: He could also speak Xianbei and likewise proclaimed orders.
translations.idiomatic: He also knew Xianbei and helped relay commands.

sentences.zh: 當煩劇之任，大見賞重。

translations.literal: Bearing arduous duties, he was greatly valued and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Given the heaviest duties, he was held in exceptional regard.

sentences.zh: 賜妻韋氏，既士人子女，又兼色貌，時人榮之。

translations.literal: He was granted Lady Wei as wife — both a scholar's daughter and possessed of beauty; men of the time counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: He was given Lady Wei in marriage — a gentleman's daughter, and beautiful besides; contemporaries envied him.

sentences.zh: 尋除左光祿大夫，常領主簿。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Left Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and regularly held the chief clerk post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made left grand master for splendid happiness while continuing as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 世宗初欲之鄴，總知朝政，高祖以其年少未許。

translations.literal: At first the heir apparent wished to go to Ye and oversee court affairs; the Grand Ancestor, because he was young, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng first wanted to go to Ye to direct government, Gao Huan would not allow it — he was still too young.

sentences.zh: 搴為致言，乃果行。

translations.literal: Cen spoke on his behalf, and it was indeed carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Cen spoke up for him, and the plan went ahead.

sentences.zh: 恃此自乞特進，世宗但加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Relying on this he himself asked for extraordinary promotion; the heir apparent only added him as irregular attendant cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: He traded on this favor and asked for extraordinary promotion; Gao Cheng only added the title irregular attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 時又大括燕、恒、雲、朔、顯、蔚、二夏州、高平、平涼之民以為軍士，逃隱者身及主人、三長、守令罪以大辟，沒入其家。

translations.literal: At the time there was again a great round-up of the people of Yan, Heng, Yun, Shuo, Xian, Yu, the two Xia provinces, Gaoping, and Pingliang as soldiers; those who fled and hid — they themselves and their masters, the three heads, and prefectural and county magistrates — were guilty of capital crime, and their households were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Another mass levy then swept the people of Yan, Heng, Yun, Shuo, Xian, Yu, the two Xia provinces, Gaoping, and Pingliang into the ranks. Anyone who hid — together with his landlord, the three heads of household organization, and local magistrates — faced execution and confiscation of the family property.

sentences.zh: 於是所獲甚衆，搴之計也。

translations.literal: Thereupon those seized were very numerous — it was Cen's plan.
translations.idiomatic: The haul was enormous; the scheme was Cen's.

sentences.zh: 搴學淺而行薄，邢邵嘗謂之曰：「更須讀書。

translations.literal: Cen's learning was shallow and his conduct thin; Xing Shao once said to him: "You need to read more.
translations.idiomatic: Cen's learning was shallow and his conduct thin. Xing Shao once told him, "You need to read more.

sentences.zh: 」搴曰：「我精騎三千，足敵君羸卒數萬。

translations.literal: " Cen said: "My three thousand picked horsemen are enough to match your tens of thousands of weakened troops.
translations.idiomatic: " Cen replied, "My three thousand picked horsemen are enough to match your tens of thousands of worn-out foot soldiers.

sentences.zh: 」嘗服棘刺丸，李諧等調之曰：「卿棘刺應自足，何假外求。

translations.literal: " He once took thorn-pill pills; Li He and others teased him, saying: "Your thorns should be enough on their own — why seek outside?
translations.idiomatic: " He once took thorn-pill medicine. Li He and others teased him, "Your thorns ought to be enough on their own — why look elsewhere?

sentences.zh: 」坐者皆笑。

translations.literal: " Those seated all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: " Those present all laughed.

sentences.zh: 司馬子如與高季式召搴飲酒，醉甚而卒，時年五十二。

translations.literal: Sima Ziru and Gao Jishi summoned Cen to drink; very drunk, he died — aged fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ziru and Gao Jishi invited Cen to drink; he drank himself to death, aged fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 高祖親臨之。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor personally attended his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan came in person to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 子如叩頭請罪，高祖曰：「折我右臂，仰覓好替還我。

translations.literal: Ziru kowtowed asking forgiveness; the Grand Ancestor said: "You have broken my right arm — look up and find me a good replacement and return him to me.
translations.idiomatic: Ziru kowtowed asking forgiveness. Gao Huan said, "You have broken my right arm — find me a good replacement and give him back.

sentences.zh: 」子如舉魏收、季式舉陳元康，以繼搴焉。

translations.literal: " Ziru recommended Wei Shou; Jishi recommended Chen Yuankang — to succeed Cen.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziru recommended Wei Shou; Jishi recommended Chen Yuankang to succeed Cen.

sentences.zh: 贈儀同三司、吏部尚書、青州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted equal in protocol to three imperators, minister of personnel, and inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously granted equal in protocol to three imperators, minister of personnel, and inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 高祖經綸大業，軍務煩廣，元康承受意旨，甚濟速用。

translations.literal: As the Grand Ancestor planned the great enterprise, military affairs were numerous and broad; Yuankang received his intent and greatly aided swift execution.
translations.idiomatic: While Gao Huan built his great enterprise amid heavy military burdens, Yuankang carried out his intent and kept affairs moving fast.

sentences.zh: 性又柔謹，通解世事。

translations.literal: By nature he was also gentle and cautious, thoroughly understanding worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and careful by nature, he understood how things worked in practice.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗怒世宗，於內親加毆蹋，極口罵之。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor once grew angry at the heir apparent and within the inner quarters personally beat and kicked him, cursing him to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan once flew into a rage at Gao Cheng and, in the inner quarters, beat and kicked him while cursing him without restraint.

sentences.zh: 出以告元康，元康諫曰：「王教訓世子，自有禮法，儀刑式瞻，豈宜至是。

translations.literal: Coming out he told Yuankang; Yuankang remonstrated, saying: "In teaching and disciplining the heir, there are ritual norms of one's own — deportment and bearing to be looked up to — how can it reach this?
translations.idiomatic: When he came out he told Yuankang. Yuankang remonstrated, "In teaching the heir there are proper ritual norms — conduct others should look up to. How can it go this far?

sentences.zh: 」言辭懇懇，至于流涕。

translations.literal: His words were earnest, even to the point of weeping.
translations.idiomatic: His words were earnest, even to tears.

sentences.zh: 高祖從此為之懲忿。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor from this restrained his anger.
translations.idiomatic: From that time Gao Huan checked his anger.

sentences.zh: 時或恚撻，輒曰：「勿使元康知之。

translations.literal: When at times he still raged and beat, he would say: "Do not let Yuankang know.
translations.idiomatic: When he still lashed out in anger, he would say, "Do not let Yuankang know.

sentences.zh: 」其敬憚如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the respect and fear he inspired.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the regard and restraint he inspired.

sentences.zh: 高仲密之叛，高祖知其由崔暹故也，將殺暹。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, the Grand Ancestor knew it was because of Cui Xuan; he was about to kill Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhongmi rebelled, Gao Huan knew Cui Xuan was the cause and meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 世宗匿而為之諫請。

translations.literal: The heir apparent hid him and pleaded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng hid him and pleaded on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「我為舍其命，須與苦手。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor said: "To spare his life I must still lay hands on him in earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "To spare his life I must still lay on a hard beating.

sentences.zh: 」世宗乃出暹而謂元康曰：「卿若使崔得杖，無相見也。

translations.literal: " The heir apparent thereupon produced Xuan and said to Yuankang: "If you let Cui be caned, we shall not meet again.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Cheng then brought Xuan out and told Yuankang, "If you let Cui be beaten, we are done with each other.

sentences.zh: 」暹在廷，解衣將受罰，元康趨入，歷階而升，且言曰：「王方以天下付大將軍，有一崔暹不能容忍耶？

translations.literal: Xuan was in the hall, removing his robe to receive punishment; Yuankang hurried in, mounting the steps in haste, and said: "My lord is about to entrust the realm to the great general — can you not tolerate one Cui Xuan?
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan stood in court stripping off his robe to take punishment. Yuankang rushed in, mounting the steps in haste, and said, "My lord is about to entrust the realm to the great general — can you not tolerate one Cui Xuan?

sentences.zh: 」高祖從而宥焉。

translations.literal: " The Grand Ancestor followed this and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan followed this and pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 世宗入輔京室，崔暹、崔季舒、崔昂等並被任使，張亮、張徽纂並高祖所待遇，然委任皆出元康之下。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent entered to assist the capital, Cui Xuan, Cui Jishu, Cui Ang, and others were all employed; Zhang Liang and Zhang Huizuan were both men the Grand Ancestor treated well — yet every commission fell short of Yuankang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng entered the capital to direct affairs, Cui Xuan, Cui Jishu, Cui Ang, and others were all employed; Zhang Liang and Zhang Huizuan were both men Gao Huan favored — yet every appointment still ranked below Yuankang.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「三崔二張，不如一康。

translations.literal: Men of the time said: "The three Cuis and two Zhangs are not the equal of one Kang.
translations.idiomatic: People said at the time, "The three Cuis and two Zhangs are not the equal of one Kang.

sentences.zh: 」魏尚書僕射范陽盧道虔女為右衛將軍郭瓊子婦，瓊以死罪沒官，高祖啟以賜元康為妻，元康乃棄故婦李氏，識者非之。

translations.literal: " Wei vice director of the masters of writing Lu Daovan of Fanyang had a daughter who was wife to Right Guards General Guo Qiong's son; Qiong was confiscated to the state on a capital charge, and the Grand Ancestor memorialized to grant her to Yuankang as wife — Yuankang thereupon abandoned his former wife, Lady Li, and men of judgment condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei vice director of the masters of writing Lu Daovan of Fanyang had a daughter married to the son of Right Guards General Guo Qiong. Qiong was condemned to death and his property seized; Gao Huan memorialized to give the woman to Yuankang as wife. Yuankang abandoned his former wife, Lady Li — and men of judgment condemned him.

sentences.zh: 元康便辟善事人，希顏候意，多有進舉，而不能平心處物，溺於財利，受納金帛，不可勝紀，放責交易，遍於州郡，為清論所譏。

translations.literal: Yuankang was skilled at winning men's favor, reading faces and awaiting intent; he made many promotions and recommendations, yet could not weigh matters with an even heart, drowning in profit — accepting gold and silk beyond counting, lending on interest and trading across commanderies and counties — and was censured by pure opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang was skilled at winning favor, reading faces and awaiting intent. He pushed many promotions, yet could not judge fairly, drowning in profit — taking bribes beyond counting, lending at interest and trading across commanderies and counties — and was censured by men of pure judgment.

sentences.zh: 從高祖破周文帝於邙山，大會諸將，議進退之策。

translations.literal: Following the Grand Ancestor in defeating Zhou Wendi at Mount Mang, he convened the generals in great assembly to deliberate advance and retreat.
translations.idiomatic: After Gao Huan defeated Yuwen Tai of Western Wei at Mount Mang, he convened the generals to debate whether to advance or withdraw.

sentences.zh: 咸以為野無青草，人馬疲瘦，不可遠追。

translations.literal: All held that in the wilds there was no fresh grass, men and horses were worn thin, and distant pursuit was impossible.
translations.idiomatic: All held that the countryside had no fresh forage, men and horses were exhausted, and distant pursuit was impossible.

sentences.zh: 元康曰：「兩雄交戰，歲月已久，今得大捷，便是天授，時不可失，必須乘勝追之。

translations.literal: Yuankang said: "Two heroes have fought for many months; to win a great victory now is heaven's gift — the moment must not be lost; we must press the victory in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang said, "Two great rivals have fought for months. To win such a victory now is heaven's gift — the moment must not be lost. We must press the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「若遇伏兵，孤何以濟？

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor said: "If we meet ambush, how shall I cross over?
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "If we meet ambush, how shall I get through?

sentences.zh: 「元康曰：「王前涉沙苑還軍，彼尚無伏，今奔敗若此，何能遠謀。

translations.literal: " Yuankang said: "When my lord before crossed Shazhi and withdrew the army, they still had no ambush; now they flee defeated like this — how can they plan far?
translations.idiomatic: " Yuankang said, "When you before crossed Shazhi and withdrew, they still laid no ambush. Now they flee in rout like this — how can they plan far ahead?

sentences.zh: 若捨而不追，必成後患。

translations.literal: If you abandon pursuit and do not chase, it will surely become a later trouble.
translations.idiomatic: If you let them go and do not pursue, it will surely breed later trouble.

sentences.zh: 」高祖竟不從。

translations.literal: " The Grand Ancestor in the end did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Huan in the end did not follow his advice.

sentences.zh: 以功封安平縣子，邑三百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed Viscount of Anping with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed viscount of Anping with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋除平南將軍、通直常侍，轉大行臺郎中，徙右丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South and regular palace attendant, transferred to gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, and moved to right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made general who pacifies the south and regular palace attendant, transferred to gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, then moved to right vice director.

sentences.zh: 及高祖疾篤，謂世宗曰：「邙山之戰，不用元康之言，方貽汝患。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor's illness grew grave, he told the heir apparent: "At the battle of Mount Mang, not using Yuankang's counsel — that is the trouble I bequeath you.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan's illness grew grave, he told Gao Cheng, "At Mount Mang, not taking Yuankang's counsel — that is the trouble I leave you.

sentences.zh: 以此為恨，死不瞑目。

translations.literal: With this as regret, I shall die with eyes unclosed.
translations.idiomatic: With this as my regret, I shall die with eyes unclosed."

sentences.zh: 」高祖崩，秘不發喪，唯元康知之。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor died, the death was kept secret and only Yuankang knew.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan died, the death was kept secret and only Yuankang knew.

sentences.zh: 世宗嗣事，又見任待。

translations.literal: The heir apparent succeeded to affairs and again showed him trust and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng succeeded to power and again showed him trust and favor.

sentences.zh: 拜散騎常侍、中軍將軍，別封昌國縣公，邑一千戶。

translations.literal: He was appointed irregular attendant cavalier and general of the central army, and additionally enfeoffed Duke of Changguo with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed irregular attendant cavalier and general of the central army, and additionally enfeoffed duke of Changguo with one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 侯景反，世宗逼於諸將，欲殺崔暹以謝之，密語元康。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing rebelled, the heir apparent, pressed by the generals, wished to kill Cui Xuan to appease them, and spoke of it secretly to Yuankang.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing rebelled, Gao Cheng, pressed by the generals, wished to kill Cui Xuan to appease them and spoke of it secretly to Yuankang.

sentences.zh: 元康諫曰：「今四海未清，綱紀已定，若以數將在外，茍悅其心，枉殺無辜，虧廢刑典，豈直上負天神，何以下安黎庶？

translations.literal: Yuankang remonstrated, saying: "The four seas are not yet tranquil and the laws are already set — if, because several generals are abroad, you would please their hearts and wrongly kill the innocent, damaging and voiding the penal code, how is it only that you fail heaven above — how can you settle the people below?
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang remonstrated, "The realm is not yet settled and the laws are in place. If, because several generals are in the field, you would please their hearts and wrongly kill the innocent, damaging the penal code — how does that only fail heaven above? How can you settle the people below?

sentences.zh: 晁錯前事，願公慎之。

translations.literal: Chao Cuo's affair of old — I beg you, sir, to be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Chao Cuo's affair of old — I beg you to be cautious.

sentences.zh: 」世宗乃止。

translations.literal: " The heir apparent thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Cheng thereupon stopped.

sentences.zh: 高岳討侯景未克，世宗欲遣潘相樂副之。

translations.literal: Gao Yue campaigned against Hou Jing without success; the heir apparent wished to send Pan Xiangyue as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yue campaigned against Hou Jing without success; Gao Cheng wished to send Pan Xiangyue as deputy.

sentences.zh: 元康曰：「相樂緩於機變，不如慕容紹宗，且先王有命，稱其堪敵侯景，公但推赤心於此人，則侯景不足憂也。

translations.literal: Yuankang said: "Xiangyue is slow in opportune change — Murong Shaozong is better; moreover the former king left a command praising him as able to match Hou Jing. My lord need only place your open heart in this man, and Hou Jing is no cause for worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang said, "Xiangyue is slow to adapt — Murong Shaozong is better. Moreover the former king left word that he could match Hou Jing. Place your full trust in this man and Hou Jing need not worry you.

sentences.zh: 」是時紹宗在遠，世宗欲召見之，恐其驚叛。

translations.literal: At the time Shaozong was far away; the heir apparent wished to summon and see him, fearing he would be alarmed into rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong was then far away; Gao Cheng wished to summon him but feared alarming him into rebellion.

sentences.zh: 元康曰：「紹宗知元康特蒙顧待，新使人來餉金，以致其誠款。

translations.literal: Yuankang said: "Shaozong knows that Yuankang enjoys special regard; he has just sent a man to present gold, to show his sincere allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang said, "Shaozong knows I enjoy special favor. He has just sent a man with gold to show his sincere allegiance.

sentences.zh: 元康欲安其意，故受之而厚答其書。

translations.literal: Yuankang wished to set his mind at ease, and therefore accepted it while replying to his letter generously.
translations.idiomatic: I wished to set his mind at ease, so I accepted it and replied generously to his letter.

sentences.zh: 保無異也。

translations.literal: Assuredly there will be no change.
translations.idiomatic: He will surely not waver.

sentences.zh: 」世宗乃任紹宗，遂以破景。

translations.literal: " The heir apparent thereupon entrusted Shaozong, and thereby broke Jing.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Cheng thereupon entrusted Shaozong, and thereby defeated Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 賞元康金五十斤。

translations.literal: Yuankang was rewarded with fifty jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang was rewarded with fifty jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 王思政入潁城，諸將攻之不能拔，元康進計於世宗曰：「公匡輔朝政，未有殊功，雖敗侯景，本非外賊。

translations.literal: Wang Sizheng entered Ying city; the generals attacked but could not take it; Yuankang offered a plan to the heir apparent, saying: "My lord assists and steadies court government, yet has no outstanding achievement; though Hou Jing was defeated, he was not a foreign foe in the first place.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng entered Ying city; the generals attacked but could not take it. Yuankang offered Gao Cheng a plan: "You assist court government yet have no outstanding achievement of your own. Though Hou Jing was defeated, he was never an outside enemy.

sentences.zh: 今潁城將陷，原公因而乘之，足以取威定業。

translations.literal: Now Ying city is about to fall — I beg my lord to take advantage and press on; that is enough to win prestige and settle your enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Now Ying is about to fall — take advantage and go in person. That is enough to win prestige and settle your enterprise.

sentences.zh: 」世宗令元康馳驛觀之。

translations.literal: " The heir apparent ordered Yuankang to ride post-horses and observe.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Cheng ordered Yuankang to ride post-horses and observe.

sentences.zh: 復命曰：「必可拔。

translations.literal: On his return he reported: "It can certainly be taken.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he reported, "It can certainly be taken.

sentences.zh: 」世宗於是親征，既至而克，賞元康金百鋌。

translations.literal: " The heir apparent thereupon campaigned in person; when he arrived it was taken, and Yuankang was rewarded with a hundred ingots of gold.
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Cheng thereupon campaigned in person; when he arrived the city fell, and Yuankang was rewarded with a hundred ingots of gold.

sentences.zh: 初，魏朝授世宗相國、齊王，世宗頻讓不受。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Wei court had offered the heir apparent the posts of chancellor of state and Prince of Qi; the heir apparent repeatedly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Wei court had offered Gao Cheng the posts of chancellor of state and Prince of Qi; he repeatedly declined.

sentences.zh: 乃召諸將及元康等密議之，諸將皆勸世宗恭應朝命，元康以為未可。

translations.literal: He thereupon summoned the generals and Yuankang and others to deliberate in secret; the generals all urged the heir apparent respectfully to accept the court command — Yuankang held it not yet possible.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned the generals and Yuankang and others to deliberate in secret. The generals all urged Gao Cheng respectfully to accept the court command — Yuankang held it not yet possible.

sentences.zh: 又謂魏收曰：「觀諸人語，專欲誤王。

translations.literal: He also said to Wei Shou: "Looking at these men's words, they mean only to mislead the prince.
translations.idiomatic: He also told Wei Shou, "Judging by what these men say, they mean only to mislead the prince.

sentences.zh: 我向已啟王，受朝命，置官僚，元康叨忝或得黃門郎，但時事未可耳。

translations.literal: I have already memorialized the prince to accept the court command and establish officials; Yuankang, unworthy, might obtain yellow gate gentleman — but the times are not yet right.
translations.idiomatic: I have already told the prince to accept the court command and establish officials — I, unworthy, might obtain yellow gate gentleman — but the times are not yet right.

sentences.zh: 」崔暹因間之，薦陸元規為大行臺郎，欲以分元康權也。

translations.literal: " Cui Xuan took advantage of the interval to recommend Lu Yuangui as gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, intending to divide Yuankang's power.
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Xuan seized the chance to recommend Lu Yuangui as gentleman of the great mobile headquarters, intending to divide Yuankang's power.

sentences.zh: 元康既貪貨賄，世宗內漸嫌之，元康頗亦自懼。

translations.literal: Yuankang being greedy for goods and bribes, the heir apparent inwardly came gradually to dislike him; Yuankang too was rather afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yuankang was greedy for bribes, Gao Cheng inwardly came to dislike him; Yuankang too grew afraid.

sentences.zh: 又欲用為中書令，以閑地處之，事未施行。

translations.literal: The heir apparent also wished to use him as director of the secretariat, placing him in an idle post — the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng also meant to make him director of the secretariat, a post that would sideline him — but the matter was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 屬世宗將受魏禪，元康與楊愔、崔季舒並在世宗坐，將大遷除朝士，共品藻之。

translations.literal: It happened that the heir apparent was about to receive the Wei abdication; Yuankang was with Yang Yin and Cui Jishu in the heir apparent's presence, about to make great transfers and dismissals of court gentlemen, jointly appraising them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Cheng was about to receive the Wei abdication, Yuankang sat with Yang Yin and Cui Jishu in his presence, about to make great transfers and dismissals of court gentlemen, jointly appraising candidates.

sentences.zh: 世宗家蒼頭奴蘭固成先掌廚膳，甚被寵昵。

translations.literal: The heir apparent's household bondservant Lan Gucheng had earlier managed the kitchen and was greatly favored and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng's household bondservant Lan Gucheng had earlier run the kitchen and was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 先是，世宗杖之數十，吳人性躁，又恃舊恩，遂大忿恚，與其同事阿改謀害世宗。

translations.literal: Earlier the heir apparent had caned him several dozen times; a man of Wu by nature impetuous, and again relying on old favor, he thereupon grew greatly resentful and with his colleague A Gai plotted to kill the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gao Cheng had beaten him several dozen times. A Wu man by nature impetuous, and again relying on old favor, he grew greatly resentful and with his colleague A Gai plotted to kill Gao Cheng.

sentences.zh: 阿改時事顯祖，常執刀隨從，云「若聞東齋叫聲」，即以加刃於顯祖。

translations.literal: A Gai then served the Manifest Ancestor, always carrying a knife in attendance, saying: "If you hear shouting from the Eastern Studio," then apply the blade to the Manifest Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: A Gai then served Gao Yang, always carrying a knife in attendance, saying, "If you hear shouting from the Eastern Studio," then turn the blade on Gao Yang.

sentences.zh: 是日值魏帝初建東宮，群官拜表。

translations.literal: That day happened to be when the Wei emperor first established the Eastern Palace and the officials all submitted memorials of congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: That day the Wei emperor had just established the Eastern Palace and officials were submitting congratulatory memorials.

sentences.zh: 事罷，顯祖出東止車門，別有所之，未還而難作。

translations.literal: When the affair ended, the Manifest Ancestor went out the Eastern Stop Chariot Gate, bound elsewhere; before he returned the calamity broke out.
translations.idiomatic: When the ceremony ended, Gao Yang went out the Eastern Stop Chariot Gate, bound elsewhere; before he returned the attack began.

sentences.zh: 固成因進食，置刀於盤下而殺世宗。

translations.literal: Gucheng thereupon came in with food, set a knife beneath the tray, and killed the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Gucheng then came in with food, set a knife beneath the tray, and killed Gao Cheng.

sentences.zh: 元康以身捍蔽，被刺傷重，至夜而終，時年四十三。

translations.literal: Yuankang used his body to shield and block; he was stabbed, his wounds grave, and died that night — aged forty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang shielded him with his body; stabbed, gravely wounded, he died that night, aged forty-three.

sentences.zh: 楊愔狼狽走出，季舒逃匿於廁，庫直紇奚舍樂捍賊死。

translations.literal: Yang Yin fled in disarray; Jishu hid in the privy; warehouse attendant Hexi Shele died defending against the assailants.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin fled in disarray; Jishu hid in the privy; warehouse attendant Hexi Shele died fighting the assailants.

sentences.zh: 是時秘世宗兇問，故殯元康於宮中，托以出使南境，虛除中書令。

translations.literal: At the time the heir apparent's violent death was kept secret; therefore Yuankang was buried within the palace, pretended to have been sent on mission to the southern border, and fictitiously appointed director of the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng's death was then kept secret; Yuankang was buried in the palace, pretended to have been sent on mission to the southern border, and fictitiously appointed director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，乃詔曰：「元康識超往哲，才極時英，千仞莫窺，萬頃難測。

translations.literal: The next year an edict said: "Yuankang's insight surpassed the sages of old, his talent the utmost of the age's heroes — a thousand fathoms none could peer into, ten thousand acres none could fathom.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict said, "Yuankang's insight surpassed the sages of old and his talent the flower of the age — a thousand fathoms none could peer into, ten thousand acres none could fathom.

sentences.zh: 綜核戎政，彌綸霸道，草昧邵陵之謀，翼贊河陽之會，運籌定策，盡力盡心，進忠補過，亡家徇國，掃平逋寇，廓清荊楚，申、甫之在隆周，子房之處盛漢，曠世同規，殊年共美。

translations.literal: He examined and regulated military government, bound and sustained hegemonic rule, drafted plans at Shaoling's founding, aided at the Henei assembly, devised strategy and settled policy, exerting heart and strength to the full, advancing loyalty and repairing faults, abandoning family and dying for the state, sweeping away fleeing bandits and clearing Jing-Chu — Shen and Fu in elevated Zhou, Zifang in flourishing Han: the same measure across ages, the same beauty across different years.
translations.idiomatic: He examined military government and sustained hegemonic rule, drafted plans at Shaoling's founding and aided at the Henei assembly, devised strategy with all his heart, advanced loyalty and repaired faults, abandoned family and died for the state, swept away fleeing bandits and cleared Jing-Chu — like Shen and Fu in elevated Zhou, like Zifang in flourishing Han: the same measure across ages, the same praise across different years.

sentences.zh: 大業未融，山隤奄及，悼傷既切，宜崇茂典。

translations.literal: The great enterprise was not yet blended; the mountain collapsed and suddenly reached him — grief and mourning being so keen, it is fitting to honor with a rich canon.
translations.idiomatic: The great enterprise was not yet complete when the mountain suddenly collapsed — grief being so keen, it is fitting to honor him with a rich canon.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、都督冀定瀛殷滄五州諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、司空公、冀州刺史，追封武邑縣一千戶，舊封並如故，諡曰文穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Ying, Yin, and Cang, grand general of agile cavalry, duke of the works, and inspector of Ji Province; posthumously enfeoffed Wuyi County with one thousand households, the former fief remaining as before — posthumous title Wemu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously granted bearer of the staff, supervisor of military affairs in Ji, Ding, Ying, Yin, and Cang provinces, grand general of agile cavalry, duke of the works, and inspector of Ji Province; posthumously enfeoffed Wuyi County with one thousand households, the former fief remaining as before — posthumous title Wemu.

sentences.zh: 賻物一千二百段。

translations.literal: Funeral goods: one thousand two hundred lengths of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral goods: one thousand two hundred lengths of silk.

sentences.zh: 大鴻臚監喪事。

translations.literal: The grand master of splendid happiness supervised the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: The grand master of splendid happiness supervised the funeral.

sentences.zh: 兇禮所須，隨由公給。

translations.literal: Whatever the funeral rites require shall be supplied from public funds as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the funeral required was to be supplied from public funds.

sentences.zh: 」元康母李氏，元康卒後，哀感發病而終，贈廣宗郡君，諡曰貞昭。

translations.literal: " Yuan Kang's mother the Lady Li, after Yuan Kang's death, grieved until illness took her and she died; posthumously granted Lady of Guangzong commandery, posthumous title Zhenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuan Kang's mother, Lady Li, after his death grieved herself into illness and died; she was posthumously granted Lady of Guangzong commandery with the posthumous title Zhenzhao.

sentences.zh: 元康子善藏，溫雅有鑒裁，武平末，假儀同三司、給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Yuan Kang's son Shancang was mild and elegant, with discerning judgment; at the end of Wuping he held acting insignia equal to three masters of ceremonies and was attendant of the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Kang's son Shancang was mild and elegant, with a keen eye for men; at the end of Wuping he held acting insignia equal to three masters of ceremonies and served as attendant of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，尚書禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was vice director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui, in the Kaihuang era, he was vice director of the ministry of rites.

sentences.zh: 大業初，卒於彭城郡贊治。

translations.literal: Early in Daye he died as superintendent of Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daye he died while serving as superintendent of Pengcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 元康弟諶，官至大鴻臚。

translations.literal: Yuan Kang's younger brother Chen reached office as grand messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Kang's younger brother Chen rose to grand messenger.

sentences.zh: 次季璩，鉅鹿太守，轉冀州別駕。

translations.literal: Next, Ji Zhuan was grand administrator of Julu, then transferred to aide-de-camp of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Next came Ji Zhuan, grand administrator of Julu, then aide-de-camp of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 平秦王歸彥反，季璩守節不從，因而遇害。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Ping'an Wang Guiyan rebelled, Ji Zhuan held to his integrity and would not follow, and was killed for it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Ping'an Wang Guiyan rebelled, Ji Zhuan held to his integrity and refused to join him, and was killed for it.

sentences.zh: 贈衛尉卿、趙州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted commandant of the guards and governor of Zhao Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted commandant of the guards and governor of Zhao Province.

sentences.zh: 杜弼，字輔玄，中山曲陽人也，小字輔國。

translations.literal: Du Bi, styled Fuxuan, was a native of Quyang in Zhongshan; his childhood name was Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: Du Bi, styled Fuxuan, came from Quyang in Zhongshan; his childhood name was Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 自序云，本京兆杜陵人，九世祖驁，晉散騎常侍，因使沒趙，遂家焉。

translations.literal: In his own preface he said he was originally from Dulang in Jingzhao; his ninth-generation ancestor Ao was Jin attendant cavalry regular and, on a mission, was lost in Zhao and settled there.
translations.idiomatic: In his own preface he said he was originally from Dulang in Jingzhao; his ninth-generation ancestor Ao had been Jin attendant cavalry regular and, on a mission, was stranded in Zhao and settled there.

sentences.zh: 祖彥衡，淮南太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yanheng was grand administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yanheng had been grand administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 父慈度，繁畤令。

translations.literal: His father Cidu was magistrate of Fanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cidu had been magistrate of Fanzhi.

sentences.zh: 弼幼聰敏，家貧無書，年十二，寄郡學受業，講授之祭，師每奇之。

translations.literal: From youth Bi was clever; the family was poor and had no books; at twelve he lodged at the district school to study, and at the sacrificial rites of instruction the teachers always marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Bi was clever; the family was poor and owned no books; at twelve he lodged at the district school. At the sacrificial rites of instruction his teachers always marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 同郡甄琛為定州長史，簡試諸生，見而策問，義解閑明，應答如響，大為琛所嘆異。

translations.literal: Fellow-district man Zhen Chen was long secretary of Ding Province; he selected and tested the students, saw Bi, and questioned him; his explanations were clear and refined and his answers came like echoes; Chen greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow townsman Zhen Chen was long secretary of Ding Province; he selected and tested students, saw Bi, and questioned him. Bi's explanations were clear and his answers came like echoes; Chen was greatly struck by him.

sentences.zh: 其子寬與弼為友。

translations.literal: Chen's son Kuan became Bi's friend.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's son Kuan became Bi's friend.

sentences.zh: 州牧任城王澄聞而召問，深相嗟賞，許以王佐之才。

translations.literal: Provincial governor Prince of Rencheng Cheng heard of him and summoned him for questioning; he deeply praised him and promised him talent fit for a king's aide.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governor Prince of Rencheng Cheng heard of him and summoned him for questioning, praised him deeply, and declared him fit to serve a king's right hand.

sentences.zh: 澄、琛還洛，稱之於朝，丞相高陽王等多相招命。

translations.literal: Cheng and Chen returned to Luoyang and praised him at court; the chancellor Prince of Gaoyang and others repeatedly invited him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Chen returned to Luoyang and praised him at court; the chancellor Prince of Gaoyang and others repeatedly sought him out.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，以軍功起家，除廣武將軍、恒州征虜府墨曹參軍，典管記。

translations.literal: In the Yan Chang era he began his career through military merit and was made general of Guangwu and clerk in the ink office of Hengzhou's expeditionary command, managing records.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yan Chang era he entered service through military merit as general of Guangwu and clerk in the ink office of Hengzhou's expeditionary command, where he managed records.

sentences.zh: 弼長於筆札，每為時輩所推。

translations.literal: Bi excelled at documents and was always recommended by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Bi excelled at documents and was always recommended by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 孝昌初，除太學博士，帶廣陽王驃騎府法曹行參軍，行臺度支郎中。

translations.literal: Early in Xiao Chang he was made erudite of the Imperial Academy, concurrently acting legal clerk in the Prince of Guangyang's rapid-cavalry office, and chief of the traveling staff's income-and-expenditure section.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xiao Chang he was made erudite of the Imperial Academy, concurrently acting legal clerk in the Prince of Guangyang's rapid-cavalry office, and chief of the traveling staff's income-and-expenditure section.

sentences.zh: 還，除光州曲城令。

translations.literal: On returning he was made magistrate of Qucheng in Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he was made magistrate of Qucheng in Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 為政清靜，務盡仁恕，詞訟止息，遠近稱之。

translations.literal: His government was quiet and clean; he strove for full humanity and clemency; lawsuits ceased, and he was praised near and far.
translations.idiomatic: His government was quiet and clean; he strove for humanity and clemency; lawsuits ceased, and he was praised near and far.

sentences.zh: 時天下多難，盜賊充斥，徵召兵役，途多亡叛，朝廷患之。

translations.literal: The age was full of troubles and bandits were everywhere; when military service was conscripted many fled and rebelled on the roads, and the court worried over it.
translations.idiomatic: The age was full of troubles and bandits were everywhere; when troops were conscripted many fled or rebelled on the roads, and the court was troubled.

sentences.zh: 乃令兵人所齎戎具，道別車載；

translations.literal: Therefore soldiers were ordered to carry their military gear, with separate carts transporting it along the road;
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers were therefore ordered to carry their own gear, with separate carts transporting it along the road;

sentences.zh: 又令縣令自送軍所。

translations.literal: magistrates were also ordered to escort their men personally to the army camp.
translations.idiomatic: magistrates were also ordered to escort their men personally to the army camp.

sentences.zh: 時光州發兵，弼送所部達北海郡，州兵一時散亡，唯弼所送不動。

translations.literal: When Guang Province sent troops, Bi escorted his district as far as Beihai commandery; the provincial soldiers scattered at once, but only those Bi escorted did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang Province sent troops, Bi escorted his district as far as Beihai commandery; the provincial soldiers scattered at once, but only the men Bi escorted held firm.

sentences.zh: 他境叛兵，並來攻劫，欲與同去。

translations.literal: Rebel soldiers from other districts all came to attack and rob them, wishing to go away together.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel soldiers from other districts came to attack and rob them, urging them to flee together.

sentences.zh: 弼率所領親兵格鬭，終莫肯從，遂得俱達軍所。

translations.literal: Bi led his personal troops to fight; in the end none would follow the rebels, and they all reached the army camp together.
translations.idiomatic: Bi led his personal troops to fight; in the end none would join the rebels, and they all reached the army camp together.

sentences.zh: 軍司崔鐘以狀上聞。

translations.literal: Army clerk Cui Zhong reported the matter upward.
translations.idiomatic: Army clerk Cui Zhong reported the matter upward.

sentences.zh: 其得人心如此。

translations.literal: Such was his winning of men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his hold on men's hearts.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，吏曹下訪守令尤異，弼已代還，東萊太守王昕以弼應訪。

translations.literal: In Pu Tai the personnel bureau sent inquiry for outstanding magistrates; Bi had already been replaced and returned, and Donglai grand administrator Wang Xin nominated Bi in response.
translations.idiomatic: In Pu Tai the personnel bureau sought outstanding magistrates; Bi had already left office and returned home, and Donglai grand administrator Wang Xin nominated him in response.

sentences.zh: 弼父在鄉，為賊所害，弼行喪六年。

translations.literal: Bi's father was in the district and was killed by bandits; Bi observed mourning for six years.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's father was in the district and was killed by bandits; Bi observed mourning for six years.

sentences.zh: 以常調除御史，加前將軍、太中大夫，領內正字。

translations.literal: Through regular assignment he was made censor, with the added titles forward general and grand master for splendid happiness, and headed the bureau's internal rectifier of characters.
translations.idiomatic: Through regular assignment he was made censor, with the added titles forward general and grand master for splendid happiness, and headed the bureau's internal rectifier of characters.

sentences.zh: 臺中彈奏，皆弼所為。

translations.literal: All impeachments in the bureau were Bi's work.
translations.idiomatic: All impeachments in the bureau were Bi's work.

sentences.zh: 諸御史出使所上文簿，委弼覆察，然後施行。

translations.literal: Memorial documents submitted by censors on missions were entrusted to Bi for review before implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Memorial documents submitted by censors on missions were entrusted to Bi for review before they were implemented.

sentences.zh: 遷中軍將軍、北豫州、驃騎大將軍府司馬。

translations.literal: He was promoted to general of the central army and staff major in the Northern Yu Province rapid-cavalry grand general's office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general of the central army and staff major in the Northern Yu Province rapid-cavalry grand general's office.

sentences.zh: 未之官，儀同竇泰總戎西伐，詔弼為泰監軍。

translations.literal: Before he took office, equal in insignia Dou Tai commanded troops on the western campaign, and an edict made Bi Dou's supervising army officer.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took office, Dou Tai, equal in insignia, commanded the western campaign, and an edict made Bi his supervising army officer.

sentences.zh: 及泰失利自殺，弼與其徒六人走還，陜州刺史劉貴鎖送晉陽。

translations.literal: When Tai was defeated and killed himself, Bi fled back with six of his men; Governor of Shan Province Liu Gui shackled and sent them to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai was defeated and killed himself, Bi fled back with six of his men; the governor of Shan Province, Liu Gui, shackled and sent them to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖詰之曰：「竇中尉此行，吾前具有法用，乃違吾語，自取敗亡。

translations.literal: Gao Huan interrogated him, saying: "Commandant Dou on this expedition — I had beforehand set out the proper use, yet he disobeyed my words and brought defeat on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan interrogated him, saying, "Commandant Dou on this expedition — I had already laid down how he was to act, yet he disobeyed my words and brought defeat on himself.

sentences.zh: 爾何由不一言諫爭也？

translations.literal: Why did you not speak a single word in remonstrance?
translations.idiomatic: Why did you not speak a single word in remonstrance?"

sentences.zh: 」弼對曰：「刀筆小生，唯文墨薄技，便宜之事，議所不及。

translations.literal: " Bi replied: "A petty clerk with brush and knife, with only slight skill in letters — on matters of convenience debate was not within my reach.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "A petty clerk with brush and knife, with only slight skill in letters — on matters of convenience debate was not within my reach."

sentences.zh: 」高祖益怒。

translations.literal: " Gao Huan grew angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan grew angrier.

sentences.zh: 賴房謨諫而獲免。

translations.literal: Thanks to Fang Mo's remonstrance he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Fang Mo's remonstrance he was spared.

sentences.zh: 左遷下灌鎮司馬。

translations.literal: He was demoted to staff major at Xia Guan garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to staff major at Xia Guan garrison.

sentences.zh: 元象初，高祖徵弼為大丞相府法曹行參軍，署記室事，轉大行臺郎中，尋加鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: Early in Yuanxiang Gao Huan summoned Bi as acting legal clerk in the great chancellor's office, assigned him to secretariat duties, transferred him to chief of the great traveling staff, and soon added general who pacifies the south.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanxiang Gao Huan summoned Bi as acting legal clerk in the great chancellor's office, assigned him to secretariat duties, made him chief of the great traveling staff, and soon added general who pacifies the south.

sentences.zh: 高祖又引弼典掌機密，甚見信待。

translations.literal: Gao Huan also brought Bi in to manage secrets and greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan also brought Bi in to manage secrets and greatly trusted him.

sentences.zh: 或有造次不及書教，直付空紙，即令宣讀。

translations.literal: Sometimes when hurried there was no time for a written instruction; he would hand blank paper and order Bi to read aloud at once.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes when hurried there was no time for a written instruction; he would hand Bi blank paper and order him to read aloud at once.

sentences.zh: 弼嘗承間密勸高祖受魏禪，高祖舉杖擊走之。

translations.literal: Bi once seized an opportunity privately to urge Gao Huan to accept the Wei abdication; Gao Huan raised his staff and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Bi once seized a private moment to urge Gao Huan to accept the Wei abdication; Gao Huan raised his staff and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 相府法曹辛子炎諮事，云須取署，子炎讀「署」為「樹」。

translations.literal: Chancellery legal clerk Xin Ziyan, on consultation matters, said they must take the signature; Ziyan read "signature" as "tree."
translations.idiomatic: Chancellery legal clerk Xin Ziyan, on a consultation matter, said they must take the signature; Ziyan read shu (signature) as shu (tree).

sentences.zh: 高祖大怒曰：「小人都不知避人家諱！

translations.literal: Gao Huan raged: "The little man does not even know to avoid another's taboo name!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan raged, "The little man does not even know to avoid another's taboo name!"

sentences.zh: 」杖之於前。

translations.literal: " He had him beaten before the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: He had him beaten before the assembly.

sentences.zh: 弼進曰：「《禮》，二名不偏諱，孔子言『征』不言『在』，言『在』不言『征』。

translations.literal: Bi advanced: "In the Rites, when there are two names one does not avoid half of either; Confucius speaking of Zheng would not say Zai, and speaking of Zai would not say Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bi advanced, "In the Rites, when there are two names one does not avoid half of either; Confucius speaking of Zheng would not say Zai, and speaking of Zai would not say Zheng.

sentences.zh: 子炎之罪，理或可恕。

translations.literal: Ziyan's crime, by reason, might be forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan's crime, by reason, might be forgiven."

sentences.zh: 」高祖罵之曰：「眼看人瞋，乃復牽經引《禮》！

translations.literal: " Gao Huan cursed him: "Seeing a man angry, you still drag in the classics and cite the Rites!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan cursed him, "Seeing a man angry, you still drag in the classics and cite the Rites!"

sentences.zh: 」叱令出去。

translations.literal: " He ordered him out with a shout.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him out with a shout.

sentences.zh: 弼行十步許，呼還，子炎亦蒙釋宥。

translations.literal: Bi had gone about ten paces when he was called back; Ziyan also received release and forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Bi had gone about ten paces when he was called back; Ziyan also received release and forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 世子在京聞之，語楊愔曰：「王左右賴有此人方正，庶天下皆蒙其利，豈獨吾家也。」

translations.literal: The heir apparent in the capital heard of it and said to Yang Yin: "At the king's side we rely on this man's uprightness; perhaps all under heaven will benefit, not our house alone."
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent in the capital heard of it and said to Yang Yin, "At the king's side we rely on this man's uprightness; perhaps all under heaven will benefit, not our house alone."

sentences.zh: 弼以文武在位，罕有廉潔，言之於高祖。

translations.literal: Because civil and military officials in office rarely had integrity, Bi spoke of it to Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Because civil and military officials in office rarely had integrity, Bi spoke of it to Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「弼來，我語爾。

translations.literal: Gao Huan said: "Bi, come — I will speak to you.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan said, "Bi, come — I will speak to you.

sentences.zh: 天下濁亂，習俗已久。

translations.literal: All under heaven is turbid and chaotic; the custom is long-standing.
translations.idiomatic: All under heaven is turbid and chaotic; the custom is long-standing.

sentences.zh: 今督將家屬多在關西，黑獺常相招誘，人情去留未定。

translations.literal: Now the supervisors' and generals' families are mostly in Guanxi; Hei La often invites and entices them, and men's hearts whether to stay or go are unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Now the supervisors' and generals' families are mostly in Guanxi; Hei La often invites and entices them, and men's hearts whether to stay or go are unsettled.

sentences.zh: 江東復有一吳兒老翁蕭衍者，專事衣冠禮樂，中原士大夫望之以為正朔所在。

translations.literal: In Jiangdong there is again an old Wu fellow, Xiao Yan, who devotes himself to caps and robes, rites and music; Central Plain scholars look to him as where the true calendar lies.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangdong there is again an old Wu fellow, Xiao Yan, who devotes himself to caps and robes, rites and music; Central Plain scholars look to him as where the true calendar lies.

sentences.zh: 我若急作法網，不相饒借，恐督將盡投黑獺，士子悉奔蕭衍，則人物流散，何以為國？

translations.literal: If I hastily make a net of law and do not spare them, I fear the supervisors and generals will all go to Hei La and the scholars all flee to Xiao Yan — then people scatter; how can there be a state?
translations.idiomatic: If I hastily make a net of law and show no forbearance, I fear the supervisors and generals will all go to Hei La and the scholars all flee to Xiao Yan — then people scatter; how can there be a state?

sentences.zh: 爾宜少待，吾不忘之。

translations.literal: You should wait a little; I do not forget this.
translations.idiomatic: You should wait a little; I do not forget this."

sentences.zh: 」及將有沙苑之役，弼又請先除內賊，卻討外寇。

translations.literal: When the Sha Yuan campaign was about to come, Bi again asked to first remove the inner traitors, then strike the outer enemies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sha Yuan campaign was about to begin, Bi again asked to remove the inner traitors first, then strike the outer enemies.

sentences.zh: 高祖問內賊是誰。

translations.literal: Gao Huan asked who the inner traitors were.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan asked who the inner traitors were.

sentences.zh: 弼曰：「諸勳貴掠奪萬民者皆是。

translations.literal: Bi said: "All the meritorious nobles who plunder the myriad people."
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "All the meritorious nobles who plunder the myriad people."

sentences.zh: 」高祖不答，因令軍人皆張弓挾矢，舉刀按矟以夾道，使弼冒出其間，曰：「必無傷也。

translations.literal: Gao Huan did not answer; he then ordered the soldiers all to draw bows with arrows nocked, raise knives, and press spears along the road, made Bi pass through among them, and said: "Surely there will be no harm."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan did not answer; he then ordered soldiers to draw bows with arrows nocked, raise knives, and press spears along the road, made Bi pass through among them, and said, "Surely there will be no harm."

sentences.zh: 」弼戰慄汗流。

translations.literal: Bi trembled in fear, sweat streaming.
translations.idiomatic: Bi trembled in fear, sweat streaming.

sentences.zh: 高祖然後喻之曰：「箭雖注，不射，刀雖舉，不擊，矟雖按，不刺，爾猶頓喪魂膽。

translations.literal: Gao Huan then explained: "Though arrows are aimed they will not shoot; though knives are raised they will not strike; though spears are pressed they will not stab — yet you still lose soul and gall utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan then explained, "Though arrows are aimed they will not shoot; though knives are raised they will not strike; though spears are pressed they will not stab — yet you still lose soul and gall utterly.

sentences.zh: 諸勳人身觸鋒刃，百死一生，縱其貪鄙，所取處大，不可同之循常例也。

translations.literal: The meritorious men touch sharp edges bodily — a hundred deaths, one life; even if their greed is base, what they take is great; they cannot be treated by the usual rule."
translations.idiomatic: The meritorious men touch sharp edges with their bodies — a hundred deaths, one life; even if their greed is base, what they take is great; they cannot be treated by the usual rule."

sentences.zh: 」弼于時大恐，因頓顙謝曰：「愚癡無智，不識至理，今蒙開曉，始見聖達之心。」

translations.literal: Bi was then greatly afraid; bowing his forehead he thanked him: "Foolish and without wisdom, not knowing the ultimate principle; now receiving enlightenment I first see the sage and penetrating mind."
translations.idiomatic: Bi was then greatly afraid; bowing his forehead he thanked him, "Foolish and without wisdom, not knowing the ultimate principle; now, enlightened, I first see the sage and penetrating mind."

sentences.zh: 後從高祖破西魏於邙山，命為露布，弼手即書絹，曾不起草。

translations.literal: Later, following Gao Huan, he defeated Western Wei at Mount Mang; ordered to compose the victory bulletin, Bi wrote on silk at once by hand without ever drafting first.
translations.idiomatic: Later, following Gao Huan, he defeated Western Wei at Mount Mang; ordered to compose the victory bulletin, Bi wrote on silk at once by hand without ever drafting first.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵定陽縣男，邑二百戶，加通直散騎常侍、中軍將軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed baron of Dingyang county with a fief of two hundred households and was added direct attendant cavalry regular and central army general.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was enfeoffed baron of Dingyang county with a fief of two hundred households and was added direct attendant cavalry regular and central army general.

sentences.zh: 奉使詣闕，魏帝見之於九龍殿，曰：「朕始讀《莊子》，便值秦名，定是體道得真，玄同齊物。

translations.literal: On mission to the court the Wei emperor saw him in the Hall of Nine Dragons and said: "When I first read the Zhuangzi I encountered the name of Qin; surely you embody the Way and attain the true, mystery same and all things equal.
translations.idiomatic: On mission to the court the Wei emperor received him in the Hall of Nine Dragons and said, "When I first read the Zhuangzi I encountered the name of Qin; surely you embody the Way and attain the true, mystery same and all things equal.

sentences.zh: 聞卿精學，聊有所問。

translations.literal: Hearing you are skilled in learning, I have a question.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing you are skilled in learning, I have a question.

sentences.zh: 經中佛性、法性為一為異？

translations.literal: In the sutras, are Buddha-nature and dharma-nature one or different?
translations.idiomatic: In the sutras, are Buddha-nature and dharma-nature one or different?"

sentences.zh: 」弼對曰：「佛性法性，止是一理。

translations.literal: " Bi replied: "Buddha-nature and dharma-nature are only one principle."
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "Buddha-nature and dharma-nature are only one principle."

sentences.zh: 」詔又問曰：「佛性既非法性，何得為一？

translations.literal: The edict again asked: "If Buddha-nature is already not dharma-nature, how can they be one?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again asked, "If Buddha-nature is already not dharma-nature, how can they be one?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「性無不在，故不說二。

translations.literal: He replied: "Nature is nowhere not present; therefore one does not speak of two."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Nature is nowhere not present; therefore one does not speak of two."

sentences.zh: 」詔又問曰：「說者皆言法性寬，佛性狹，寬狹既別，非二如何？

translations.literal: The edict again asked: "Speakers all say dharma-nature is broad and Buddha-nature narrow; broad and narrow already distinct — if not two, how?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again asked, "Speakers all say dharma-nature is broad and Buddha-nature narrow; broad and narrow are already distinct — if not two, how?"

sentences.zh: 」弼又對曰：「在寬成寬，在狹成狹，若論性體，非寬非狹。

translations.literal: Bi again replied: "In the broad it becomes broad, in the narrow it becomes narrow; if one discusses the substance of nature, it is neither broad nor narrow."
translations.idiomatic: Bi again replied, "In the broad it becomes broad, in the narrow it becomes narrow; if one discusses the substance of nature, it is neither broad nor narrow."

sentences.zh: 」詔問曰：「既言成寬成狹，何得非寬非狹？

translations.literal: The edict asked: "Since you say it becomes broad and becomes narrow, how can it be neither broad nor narrow?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Since you say it becomes broad and becomes narrow, how can it be neither broad nor narrow?

sentences.zh: 若定是狹，亦不能成寬。

translations.literal: If fixed as narrow, it also cannot become broad."
translations.idiomatic: If fixed as narrow, it also cannot become broad."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「以非寬狹，故能成寬狹，寬狹所成雖異，能成恒一。

translations.literal: He replied: "Because it is not broad or narrow, therefore it can become broad or narrow; what broad and narrow become may differ, but what can become is constantly one."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Because it is not broad or narrow, therefore it can become broad or narrow; what broad and narrow become may differ, but what can become is constantly one."

sentences.zh: 」上悅稱善。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and praised it as good.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and praised it as good.

sentences.zh: 乃引入經書庫，賜《地持經》一部，帛一百匹。

translations.literal: He then led him into the sutra library and granted one copy of the Dizhi Sutra and one hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He then led him into the sutra library and granted one copy of the Dizhi Sutra and one hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 平陽公淹為幷州刺史，高祖又命弼帶幷州驃騎府長史。

translations.literal: Prince of Pingyang Yan was governor of Bing Province; Gao Huan also ordered Bi concurrently as chief clerk of Bing's rapid-cavalry office.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pingyang Yan was governor of Bing Province; Gao Huan also ordered Bi to serve concurrently as chief clerk of Bing's rapid-cavalry office.

sentences.zh: 弼性好名理，探味玄宗，自在軍旅，帶經從役。

translations.literal: By nature Bi loved subtle principle and tasted the profundities of the Way; from his time in the army he carried sutras on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Bi loved subtle principle and tasted the profundities of the Way; from his time in the army he carried sutras on campaign.

sentences.zh: 註老子《道德經》二卷，表上之曰：「臣聞乘風理弋，追逸羽於高雲；

translations.literal: He annotated Laozi's Daode Jing in two juan and memorialized: "Your servant has heard that riding the wind one adjusts the arrow and pursues swift feathers in high clouds;
translations.idiomatic: He annotated Laozi's Daode Jing in two juan and memorialized, "Your servant has heard that riding the wind one adjusts the arrow and pursues swift feathers in high clouds;

sentences.zh: 臨波命鉤，引沈鱗於大壑。

translations.literal: standing by the wave one commands the hook and draws submerged scales from the great abyss.
translations.idiomatic: standing by the wave one commands the hook and draws submerged scales from the great abyss.

sentences.zh: 茍得其道，為工其事，在物既爾，理亦固然。

translations.literal: If one obtains its Way one masters the work; in things it is so, in principle likewise naturally so.
translations.idiomatic: If one obtains its Way one masters the work; in things it is so, in principle likewise naturally so.

sentences.zh: 竊惟《道》、《德》二經，闡明幽極，旨冥動寂，用周凡聖。

translations.literal: I venture to consider the two classics Dao and De — they illuminate the dark utmost; their purport is dark in motion and stillness; their use pervades common and sage.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to consider the two classics Dao and De — they illuminate the dark utmost; their purport is dark in motion and stillness; their use pervades common and sage.

sentences.zh: 論行也，清凈柔弱，語跡也成功致治。

translations.literal: Speaking of practice: pure, quiet, soft and yielding; speaking of traces: success and achieving order.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of practice: pure, quiet, soft and yielding; speaking of traces: success and achieving order.

sentences.zh: 實衆流之江海，乃群藝之本根。

translations.literal: Truly the Yangtze and sea among all streams, the root of all arts.
translations.idiomatic: Truly the Yangtze and sea among all streams, the root of all arts.

sentences.zh: 臣少覽經書，偏所篤好，雖從役軍府，而不舍遊息。

translations.literal: Your servant from youth browsed sutras and was especially devoted; though serving in the army office he did not abandon leisure pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant from youth browsed sutras and was especially devoted; though serving in the army office he did not abandon leisure pursuit.

sentences.zh: 鉆味既久，斐斖如有所見，比之前註，微謂異於舊說。

translations.literal: Drilling into the flavor long, patterns emerged as if he had insight; compared with earlier commentaries he slightly judged them different from the old doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Drilling into the flavor long, patterns emerged as if he had insight; compared with earlier commentaries he slightly judged them different from the old doctrine.

sentences.zh: 情發於中而彰諸外，輕以管窺，遂成穿鑿。

translations.literal: Feeling arising within and manifesting without, lightly using a tube to peer, thus became forced interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: Feeling arising within and manifesting without, lightly using a tube to peer, he thus produced forced interpretation.

sentences.zh: 無取於遊刃，有慚於運斤。

translations.literal: No borrowing from the roaming blade; shame before the wielding axe.
translations.idiomatic: No borrowing from the roaming blade; shame before the wielding axe."

sentences.zh: 不足破秋毫之論，何以解連環之結。

translations.literal: Arguments not equal to splitting an autumn down — how can they untie the linked rings?
translations.idiomatic: If the reasoning cannot match the finest hair-splitting, how can it loosen the linked rings?

sentences.zh: 本欲止於門內，貽厥童蒙，兼以近資愚鄙，私備忘闕。

translations.literal: Originally I meant to keep this within my own gate, to leave it for children in their first studies, and also to assist my own foolishness close at hand, privately to fill gaps in memory.
translations.idiomatic: I had meant to keep this within my own household, to leave it for children at their first lessons, and also to shore up my own dullness nearby, privately filling gaps in what I remembered.

sentences.zh: 不悟姑射凝神，汾陽流照，蓋高之聽卑，邇言在察。

translations.literal: I did not realize that on Mount Guye the spirit gathers, that Fenyang streams its radiance — the high listens to the low, and words spoken near at hand are to be examined.
translations.idiomatic: I did not grasp that on Mount Guye the spirit gathers, that Fenyang sends down its light — the lofty hears the humble, and what is said close at hand must be scrutinized.

sentences.zh: 春末奉旨，猥蒙垂誘，今上所註《老子》，謹冒封呈，並序如別。

translations.literal: Late in spring I received the edict and was humbly favored with encouragement; the present sovereign's commentary on the Laozi — I respectfully dare to present it sealed, with a preface as a separate document.
translations.idiomatic: Late in spring I received the edict and was graciously encouraged; the present sovereign's commentary on the Laozi — I respectfully present it sealed, with a preface submitted separately.

sentences.zh: 」詔答云：「李君遊神冥窅，獨觀恍惚，玄同造化，宗羣極群有。

translations.literal: " The edict replied: "Master Li roams the spirit in dark obscurity, alone contemplates the dim and vague, is mysteriously one with creation, and takes the multitude of beings as his end.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict replied: "Master Li roams the spirit in the dark void, alone contemplates the dim and vague, is mysteriously one with creation, and takes the multitude of beings as his end.

sentences.zh: 從中被外，周應可以裁成；

translations.literal: From within reaching the outer, a comprehensive response can trim and form;
translations.idiomatic: From within reaching outward, a comprehensive response can shape and complete;

sentences.zh: 自己及物，運行可以資用。

translations.literal: from the self to things, operation can supply use.
translations.idiomatic: from the self to things, operation can supply what is needed.

sentences.zh: 隆家寧國，義屬斯文。

translations.literal: Elevating the family and pacifying the state — the meaning belongs to this learning.
translations.idiomatic: To exalt the house and settle the realm — that meaning belongs to this learning.

sentences.zh: 卿才思優洽，業尚通遠，息棲儒門，馳騁玄肆，既啟專家之學，且暢釋老之言。

translations.literal: Your talent and thought are excellent and thorough; your pursuits are lofty and far-reaching. You rested in the Confucian gate and galloped in the Daoist market — you have both opened specialized learning and expounded the teachings of Buddhism and Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: Your talent and thought are excellent and thorough; your pursuits are lofty and far-reaching. You rested in the Confucian gate and ranged through the Daoist hall — you have both opened a school of your own and made plain the teachings of Buddhism and Laozi.

sentences.zh: 戶列門張，途通徑達，理事兼申，能用俱表，彼賢所未悟，遺老所未聞，旨極精微，言窮深妙。

translations.literal: Households arrayed, gates open; paths connected, routes direct — principle and affairs both expressed, ability and use both displayed. What those worthies had not awakened to, what old recluses had not heard — the aim is utmost subtlety, the words exhaust depth and wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Households arrayed, gates open; paths connected, routes direct — principle and affairs both set forth, ability and use both shown. What those worthies had not grasped, what old recluses had not heard — the aim is utmost subtlety, the words exhaust depth and wonder.

sentences.zh: 朕有味二經，倦於舊說，歷覽新註，所得已多，嘉尚之來，良非一緒。

translations.literal: We have taste for the two classics and are weary of old explanations; having reviewed new commentaries, our gain is already great — the esteem we feel comes from more than one source.
translations.idiomatic: We relish the two classics and are weary of old explanations; having reviewed new commentaries, our gain is already great — the esteem we feel does not spring from one cause alone.

sentences.zh: 已勑殺青編，藏之延閣。

translations.literal: We have already ordered it bound in green silk and stored in the Yan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: We have already ordered it bound in green silk and stored in the Yan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 」又上一本於高祖，一本於世宗。

translations.literal: " He also presented one copy to Gao Huan and one to Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: " He also presented one copy to Gao Huan and one to Shizong.

sentences.zh: 武定中，遷衛尉卿。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was promoted to Commandant of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wuding era he was promoted to commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 會梁遣貞陽侯蕭明等入寇彭城，大都督高岳、行臺慕容紹宗率諸軍討之，詔弼為軍司，攝行臺左丞。

translations.literal: When Liang sent the Marquis of Zhenyang, Xiao Ming, and others to invade Pengcheng, Grand Commander Gao Yue and the expeditionary force Murong Shaozong led the armies to attack them; an edict made Bi army adjutant and acting left director of the expeditionary secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang sent the Marquis of Zhenyang, Xiao Ming, and others to invade Pengcheng, Grand Commander Gao Yue and expeditionary commander Murong Shaozong led the armies against them; an edict appointed Bi army adjutant and acting left director of the expeditionary secretariat.

sentences.zh: 臨發，世宗賜胡馬一匹，語弼曰：「此廄中第二馬，孤恒自乘騎，今方遠別，聊以為贈。

translations.literal: Before departure Shizong gave him a Hu horse and said to Bi: "This is the second horse in the stable; I always ride it myself. Now that we part far apart, I offer it to you in passing.
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out, Shizong gave him a Hu horse and said to Bi, "This is the second horse in the stable; I always ride it myself. Now that we part for a distant campaign, I offer it to you in passing.

sentences.zh: 」又令陳政務之要可為鑒戒者，錄一兩條。

translations.literal: " He also ordered him to record one or two points of important administration that could serve as mirrors and warnings.
translations.idiomatic: " He also ordered him to set down one or two points of important administration that could serve as mirrors and warnings.

sentences.zh: 弼請口陳曰：「天下大務，莫過賞罰二端，賞一人使天下人喜，罰一人使天下人服。

translations.literal: Bi asked to state them orally: "Under Heaven's great tasks, nothing surpasses reward and punishment; reward one man and all under Heaven rejoice, punish one man and all under Heaven submit.
translations.idiomatic: Bi asked to state them orally: "Under Heaven's great tasks, nothing surpasses reward and punishment; reward one man and all under Heaven rejoice, punish one man and all under Heaven submit.

sentences.zh: 但能二事得中，自然盡美。

translations.literal: If only these two matters hit the mark, beauty is naturally complete.
translations.idiomatic: If only these two are kept true, perfection follows of itself.

sentences.zh: 」世宗大悅曰：「言雖不多，於理甚要。

translations.literal: " Shizong was greatly pleased and said: "Your words are not many, but in principle they are very important.
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong was greatly pleased and said, "Your words are few, but in principle they matter greatly.

sentences.zh: 」握手而別。

translations.literal: " They clasped hands and parted.
translations.idiomatic: " They clasped hands and parted.

sentences.zh: 破蕭明於寒山，別與領軍潘樂攻拔梁潼州，仍與岳等撫軍恤民，合境傾賴。

translations.literal: They defeated Xiao Ming at Hanshan; separately, with army commander Pan Yue, Bi attacked and took Liang's Tong Prefecture, and still with Yue and the others comforted the army and pitied the people — the whole circuit relied on them.
translations.idiomatic: They defeated Xiao Ming at Hanshan; separately, with army commander Pan Yue, Bi attacked and took Liang's Tong Prefecture, and still with Yue and the others comforted the troops and showed mercy to the people — the whole circuit leaned on them.

sentences.zh: 六年四月八日，魏帝集名僧於顯陽殿講說佛理，弼與吏部尚書楊愔、中書令邢邵、秘書監魏收等並侍法筵。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the fourth month of the sixth year, the Wei emperor gathered famed monks at the Xianyang Hall to expound Buddhist doctrine; Bi, together with Minister of Personnel Yang Yin, Secretariat Director Xing Shao, Secretariat Supervisor Wei Shou, and others, all attended the dharma mat.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the fourth month of the sixth year, the Wei emperor gathered famed monks at the Xianyang Hall to expound Buddhist doctrine; Bi, together with Minister of Personnel Yang Yin, Secretariat Director Xing Shao, Secretariat Supervisor Wei Shou, and others, all attended the dharma mat.

sentences.zh: 敕弼升師子座，當衆敷演。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Bi to ascend the lion seat and expound before the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Bi to ascend the lion seat and expound before the assembly.

sentences.zh: 昭玄都僧達及僧道順並緇林之英，問難鋒至，往復數十番，莫有能屈。

translations.literal: Zhaoxuan Director of Monks Da and the monk Daoshun, both eminent in the black-robed forest, pressed questions like blades; back and forth for several dozen rounds, none could overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoxuan Director of Monks Da and the monk Daoshun, both eminent in the sangha, pressed questions like blades; back and forth for several dozen rounds, none could overcome him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此賢若生孔門，則何如也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If this worthy had been born at Confucius's gate, then what?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If this worthy had been born at Confucius's gate, then what?"

sentences.zh: 關中遣儀同王思政據潁州，太尉高岳等攻之。

translations.literal: Guanzhong sent Yitong Wang Sizheng to hold Ying Prefecture; Grand Marshal Gao Yue and others attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong sent Yitong Wang Sizheng to hold Ying Prefecture; Grand Marshal Gao Yue and others attacked him.

sentences.zh: 弼行潁州事，攝行臺左丞。

translations.literal: Bi handled the affairs of Ying Prefecture and acted as left director of the expeditionary secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Bi handled the affairs of Ying Prefecture and acted as left director of the expeditionary secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時大軍在境，調輸多費，弼均其苦樂，公私兼舉，大為州民所稱。

translations.literal: At that time the great army was in the territory and levies cost much; Bi balanced suffering and joy, and both public and private interests were advanced — the people of the prefecture praised him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the great army was in the territory and levies cost dearly; Bi balanced hardship and ease, and both public and private interests were served — the people of the prefecture praised him greatly.

sentences.zh: 潁州之平也，世宗曰：「卿試論王思政所以被擒。

translations.literal: When Ying Prefecture was pacified, Shizong said: "Try discussing the reason Wang Sizheng was captured."
translations.idiomatic: When Ying Prefecture was pacified, Shizong said, "Tell me why Wang Sizheng was captured."

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「思政不察逆順之理，不識大小之形，不度強弱之勢，有此三蔽，宜其俘獲。

translations.literal: Bi said: "Sizheng did not examine the principle of rebellion and obedience, did not know the forms of great and small, and did not measure the situation of strong and weak — with these three blind spots, capture was fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Bi said, "Sizheng did not examine the principle of rebellion and obedience, did not know the forms of great and small, and did not measure the situation of strong and weak — with these three blind spots, capture was fitting."

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「古有逆取順守，大吳困於小越，弱燕能破強齊。

translations.literal: " Shizong said: "In antiquity there was taking by rebellion and guarding by obedience; great Wu was trapped by small Yue, and weak Yan could break strong Qi.
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong said, "In antiquity there was taking by rebellion and guarding by obedience; great Wu was trapped by small Yue, and weak Yan could break strong Qi.

sentences.zh: 卿之三義，何以自立？

translations.literal: Your three points — how do they stand?"
translations.idiomatic: Your three points — how do they stand?"

sentences.zh: 「弼曰：「王若順而不大，大而不強，強而不順，於義或偏，得如聖旨。

translations.literal: " Bi said: "If a king is obedient but not great, great but not strong, or strong but not obedient, in principle he may be partial and would not match the sage's intent.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "If a king is obedient but not great, great but not strong, or strong but not obedient, in principle he may be partial and would not match the sage's intent.

sentences.zh: 今既兼備衆勝，鄙言可以還立。

translations.literal: Now that all victories are combined, my crude words can stand again."
translations.idiomatic: Now that all victories are combined, my crude words can stand again."

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「凡欲持論，宜有定指，那得廣包衆理，欲以多端自固？

translations.literal: " Shizong said: "Generally, in holding a debate one ought to have a fixed aim — how can one broadly wrap up every principle and try to secure oneself by many ends?"
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong said, "In debate one ought to have a fixed aim — how can one wrap up every principle and try to secure oneself with many arguments?"

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「大王威德，事兼衆美，義博故言博，非義外施言。

translations.literal: " Bi said: "Great King's prestige and virtue combine every excellence; meaning is broad, so words are broad — it is not applying words outside the meaning."
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "Great King's prestige and virtue combine every excellence; meaning is broad, so words are broad — it is not piling words beyond the meaning."

sentences.zh: 」世宗曰：「若爾，何故周年不下，孤來即拔？

translations.literal: " Shizong said: "If so, why was it not taken in a full year, yet when I came it fell at once?"
translations.idiomatic: " Shizong said, "If so, why was it not taken in a full year, yet when I came it fell at once?"

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「此蓋天意欲顯大王之功。」

translations.literal: " Bi said: "This was surely Heaven's intent wanting to display Great King's merit."
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "This was surely Heaven's intent wanting to display Great King's merit."

sentences.zh: 顯祖引為兼長史，加衛將軍，轉中書令，仍長史。
