translations.literal: Xianzu summoned him as concurrent chief administrator, added Guard General, transferred him to Secretariat Director, and he still served as chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu summoned him as concurrent chief administrator, added guard general, transferred him to secretariat director, and he still served as chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 進爵定陽縣侯，增邑通前五百戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced in enfeoffment to Marquis of Dingyang, with a fief combined with the previous grant reaching five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced in enfeoffment to marquis of Dingyang, with a fief combined with the previous grant reaching five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 弼志在匡贊，知無不為。

translations.literal: Bi's aim was to support and aid; there was nothing he knew of that he did not do.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's aim was to support and aid; there was nothing he knew of that he did not do.

sentences.zh: 顯祖將受魏禪，自晉陽至平城都，命弼與司空司馬子如馳驛先入，觀察物情。

translations.literal: When Xianzu was about to receive the Wei abdication, traveling from Jinyang to the capital at Pingcheng, he ordered Bi and Sikong Sima Ziru's son Ziru to ride post-horses in advance and observe the people's feelings.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzu was about to receive the Wei abdication, traveling from Jinyang to the capital at Pingcheng, he ordered Bi and Sikong Sima Ziru's son Ziru to ride post-horses in advance and observe the people's feelings.

sentences.zh: 踐祚之後，敕命左右箱入柏閣。

translations.literal: After he took the throne, an edict ordered the left and right document boxes brought into the Cypress Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After he took the throne, an edict ordered the left and right document boxes brought into the Cypress Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 以預定策之功，遷驃騎將軍、衛尉卿，別封長安縣伯。

translations.literal: For merit in deciding policy, he was promoted to Flying Cavalry General and Commandant of the Guards, and was separately enfeoffed as Baron of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in deciding policy, he was promoted to flying cavalry general and commandant of the guards, and was separately enfeoffed as baron of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 嘗與邢卲扈從東山，共論名理。

translations.literal: Once, attending Xianzu on the Eastern Mountain together with Xing Shao, they discussed essential principles.
translations.idiomatic: Once, attending Xianzu on the Eastern Mountain together with Xing Shao, they discussed essential principles.

sentences.zh: 邢以為人死還生，恐為蛇畫足。

translations.literal: Xing held that when a man dies he returns to life — he feared drawing feet on a snake.
translations.idiomatic: Xing held that when a man dies he returns to life — he feared drawing feet on a snake.

sentences.zh: 弼答曰：「蓋謂人死歸無，非有能生之力。

translations.literal: Bi replied: "Generally this means that when a man dies he returns to nothing and has no power to give life.
translations.idiomatic: Bi replied, "Generally this means that when a man dies he returns to nothing and has no power to give life.

sentences.zh: 然物之未生，本亦無也，無而能有，不以為疑，因前生後，何獨致怪？

translations.literal: Yet things not yet born originally had no existence either; from nothing can come being — this is not regarded as doubtful. From a prior life to a later life, why alone cause wonder?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet things not yet born originally had no existence either; from nothing can come being — this is not regarded as doubtful. From a prior life to a later life, why alone cause wonder?"

sentences.zh: 」邢云：「聖人設教，本由勸獎，故懼以將來，理望各遂其性。

translations.literal: " Xing said: "The sages set up teaching fundamentally to encourage and reward; therefore they use fear of what is to come so that each may attain his nature as principle hopes."
translations.idiomatic: " Xing said, "The sages set up teaching fundamentally to encourage and reward; therefore they use fear of what is to come so that each may attain his nature as principle hopes."

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「聖人合德天地，齊信四時，言則為經，行則為法，而雲以虛示物，以詭勸民，將同魚腹之書，有異鑿楹之誥，安能使北辰降光，龍宮韞櫝。

translations.literal: " Bi said: "The sages combine virtue with Heaven and Earth and equal trust to the four seasons; their speech becomes the classic and their conduct becomes law — yet you say they use emptiness to show things and deceit to encourage the people. That would be like the book in the fish's belly and unlike the edict drilled into the pillar — how could the North Star send down its light and the dragon palace hold its casket?
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "The sages combine virtue with Heaven and Earth and equal trust to the four seasons; their speech becomes the classic and their conduct becomes law — yet you say they use emptiness to show things and deceit to encourage the people. That would be like the book in the fish's belly and unlike the edict drilled into the pillar — how could the North Star send down its light and the dragon palace hold its casket?

sentences.zh: 就如所論，福果可以熔鑄性靈，弘獎風教，為益之大，莫極於斯。

translations.literal: Just as in your discussion, reward and fruit can melt and cast the nature of the spirit and greatly encourage moral teaching — in benefit nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Just as in your discussion, reward and fruit can melt and cast the nature of the spirit and greatly encourage moral teaching — in benefit nothing surpasses this.

sentences.zh: 此既真教，何謂非實？

translations.literal: This is true teaching; why call it unreal?"
translations.idiomatic: This is true teaching; why call it unreal?"

sentences.zh: 」邢云：「死之言『澌』，精神盡也。

translations.literal: " Xing said: "In speaking of death, 'si' means the spirit is exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: " Xing said, "In speaking of death, 'si' means the spirit is exhausted."

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「此所言澌，如射箭盡，手中盡也。

translations.literal: " Bi said: "This 'si' is like an arrow shot to exhaustion — the hand is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "This 'si' is like an arrow shot to exhaustion — the hand is exhausted.

sentences.zh: 《小雅》曰『無草不死』，《月令》又云 『靡草死』，動植雖殊，亦此之類。

translations.literal: The Xiaoya says 'no grass does not die,' and the Monthly Ordinances also says 'decaying grass dies' — plants that move and plants that stand differ, yet they belong to the same category.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiaoya says 'no grass does not die,' and the Monthly Ordinances also says 'decaying grass dies' — plants that move and plants that stand differ, yet they belong to the same category.

sentences.zh: 無情之卉，尚得還生，含靈之物，何妨再造。

translations.literal: Unfeeling plants can still return to life; things that hold spirit — why should re-creation be hindered?
translations.idiomatic: Unfeeling plants can still return to life; things that hold spirit — why should re-creation be hindered?

sentences.zh: 若云草死猶有種在，則復人死亦有識。

translations.literal: If you say that when grass dies seed still remains within, then again when a man dies there is also consciousness.
translations.idiomatic: If you say that when grass dies seed still remains within, then again when a man dies there is also consciousness.

sentences.zh: 識種不見，謂以為無者。

translations.literal: Seed and consciousness are not seen and are therefore called nonexistent.
translations.idiomatic: Seed and consciousness are not seen and are therefore called nonexistent.

sentences.zh: 神之在形，亦非自矚，離朱之明不能睹。

translations.literal: Spirit in the form is also not self-visible; even Li Zhu's brightness cannot see it.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit in the form is also not self-visible; even Li Zhu's brightness cannot see it.

sentences.zh: 雖孟軻觀眸，賢愚可察；

translations.literal: Though Mencius could examine the pupils, worthy and foolish could be distinguished;
translations.idiomatic: Though Mencius could examine the pupils, worthy and foolish could be distinguished;

sentences.zh: 鐘生聽曲，山水呈狀。

translations.literal: Zhong You, hearing music, made mountains and waters appear in form —
translations.idiomatic: Zhong You, hearing music, made mountains and waters appear in form —

sentences.zh: 乃神之工，豈神之質。

translations.literal: yet these are the spirit's workmanship; how are they the spirit's substance?
translations.idiomatic: yet these are the spirit's workmanship; how are they the spirit's substance?

sentences.zh: 猶玉帛之非禮，鐘鼓之非樂，以此而推，義斯見矣。

translations.literal: It is like jade and silk not being ritual, or bells and drums not being music; push from this and the meaning is seen."
translations.idiomatic: It is like jade and silk not being ritual, or bells and drums not being music; push from this and the meaning is seen."

sentences.zh: 」邢云：「季札言無不之，亦言散盡，若復聚而為物，不得言無不之也。

translations.literal: " Xing said: "When Ji Zha said 'nothing does not go,' he also meant scattered exhaustion; if it gathers again to become a thing, one cannot say 'nothing does not go.'"
translations.idiomatic: " Xing said, "When Ji Zha said 'nothing does not go,' he also meant scattered exhaustion; if it gathers again to become a thing, one cannot say 'nothing does not go.'"

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「骨肉下歸於土，魂氣則無不之，此乃形墜魂遊，往而非盡。

translations.literal: " Bi said: "Flesh and bone below return to earth, while soul and breath then have nowhere they do not go — this is the form fallen and the soul roaming; gone, yet not exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "Flesh and bone below return to earth, while soul and breath then have nowhere they do not go — this is the form fallen and the soul roaming; gone, yet not exhausted.

sentences.zh: 如鳥出巢，如蛇出穴。

translations.literal: It is like a bird leaving the nest or a snake leaving its hole.
translations.idiomatic: It is like a bird leaving the nest or a snake leaving its hole.

sentences.zh: 由其尚有，故無所不之，若令無也，之將焉適？

translations.literal: Because something still exists, there is nowhere it does not go; if you make it nothing, where would it go?
translations.idiomatic: Because something still exists, there is nowhere it does not go; if you make it nothing, where would it go?

sentences.zh: 延陵有察微之識，知其不隨於形；

translations.literal: Yanling had the knowledge to discern the subtle and knew that it does not follow the form;
translations.idiomatic: Yanling had the knowledge to discern the subtle and knew that it does not follow the form;

sentences.zh: 仲尼發習禮之嘆，美其斯與形別。

translations.literal: Confucius uttered a sigh at studying the rites and praised that it differs from the form.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius uttered a sigh at studying the rites and praised that it differs from the form.

sentences.zh: 若許以廓然，然則人皆季子。

translations.literal: If you permit the broad and empty, then everyone would be Ji Zi.
translations.idiomatic: If you permit the broad and empty, then everyone would be Ji Zi.

sentences.zh: 不謂高論，執此為無。

translations.literal: This is not called lofty discourse — to hold this as nothing."
translations.idiomatic: This is not called lofty discourse — to hold this as nothing."

sentences.zh: 」邢云：「神之在人，猶光之在燭，燭盡則光窮，人死則神滅。

translations.literal: " Xing said: "Spirit in a person is like light in a candle; when the candle is exhausted the light ends, and when the person dies the spirit perishes."
translations.idiomatic: " Xing said, "Spirit in a person is like light in a candle; when the candle is exhausted the light ends, and when the person dies the spirit perishes."

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「舊學前儒，每有斯語，群疑衆惑，咸由此起。

translations.literal: " Bi said: "The old learning and former Confucians have this saying every time; the crowd's doubts and the multitude's confusions all arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "The old learning and former Confucians repeat this saying; the crowd's doubts and the multitude's confusions all arise from this.

sentences.zh: 蓋辨之者未精，思之者不篤。

translations.literal: Generally, those who discriminate are not refined and those who think are not earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Generally, those who discriminate are not refined and those who think are not earnest.

sentences.zh: 竊有末見，可以覈諸。

translations.literal: I have a slight point not yet seen that can be verified thereby.
translations.idiomatic: I have a slight point not yet seen that can be verified thereby.

sentences.zh: 燭則因質生光，質大光亦大；

translations.literal: A candle generates light because of its substance; the larger the substance, the larger the light.
translations.idiomatic: A candle generates light because of its substance; the larger the substance, the larger the light.

sentences.zh: 人則神不系於形，形小神不小。

translations.literal: A person is not one whose spirit is tied to the form; the smaller the form, the spirit is not smaller.
translations.idiomatic: A person is not one whose spirit is tied to the form; the smaller the form, the spirit is not smaller.

sentences.zh: 故仲尼之智，必不短於長狄；

translations.literal: Thus Confucius's wisdom was certainly not shorter than the Long Di's;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Confucius's wisdom was certainly not shorter than the Long Di's;

sentences.zh: 孟德之雄，乃遠奇於崔琰。

translations.literal: Cao Cao's heroism was far beyond Cui Yan's.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao's heroism was far beyond Cui Yan's.

sentences.zh: 神之於形，亦猶君之有國。

translations.literal: Spirit to form is also like a lord having a state.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit to form is also like a lord having a state.

sentences.zh: 國實君之所統，君非國之所生。

translations.literal: The state is truly what the lord governs; the lord is not what the state gives birth to.
translations.idiomatic: The state is truly what the lord governs; the lord is not what the state gives birth to.

sentences.zh: 不與同生，孰云俱滅？

translations.literal: Not born together — who says they perish together?"
translations.idiomatic: Not born together — who says they perish together?"

sentences.zh: 』邢云：「舍此適彼，生生恒在。

translations.literal: " Xing said: "Leaving this and adapting to that — birth upon birth is always present.
translations.idiomatic: " Xing said, "Leaving this and adapting to that — birth upon birth is always present.

sentences.zh: 周、孔自應同莊周之鼓缶，和桑扈之循歌？

translations.literal: Should Zhou and Confucius not be the same as Zhuang Zhou drumming on a pot and harmonizing with Sanghu's following song?"
translations.idiomatic: Should Zhou and Confucius not be the same as Zhuang Zhou drumming on a pot and harmonizing with Sanghu's following song?"

sentences.zh: 「弼曰：「共陰而息，尚有將別之悲；

translations.literal: " Bi said: "Sharing shade and resting still has the sorrow of impending parting;
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "Sharing shade and resting still has the sorrow of impending parting;

sentences.zh: 窮轍以遊，亦與中途之嘆。

translations.literal: driving an exhausted cart to roam also has the sigh of mid-journey.
translations.idiomatic: driving an exhausted cart to roam also has the sigh of mid-journey.

sentences.zh: 況曰聯體同氣，化為異物，稱情之服，何害於聖。

translations.literal: How much more when bodies joined and breath shared are transformed into different things — mourning suited to feeling; what harm to a sage?"
translations.idiomatic: How much more when bodies joined and breath shared are transformed into different things — mourning suited to feeling; what harm to a sage?"

sentences.zh: 」邢云：「鷹化為鳩，鼠變為鴽，黃母為鱉，皆是生之類也。

translations.literal: " Xing said: "A hawk transforms into a dove, a rat changes into a quail, and a yellow mother into a turtle — all are categories of birth.
translations.idiomatic: " Xing said, "A hawk transforms into a dove, a rat changes into a quail, and a yellow mother into a turtle — all are categories of birth.

sentences.zh: 類化而相生，猶光去此燭，復然彼燭。

translations.literal: Categories transform yet give birth to one another, like light leaving this candle and again igniting that candle."
translations.idiomatic: Categories transform yet give birth to one another, like light leaving this candle and again igniting that candle."

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「鷹未化為鳩，鳩則非有。

translations.literal: " Bi said: "Before the hawk has transformed into a dove, the dove does not exist.
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "Before the hawk has transformed into a dove, the dove does not exist.

sentences.zh: 鼠既二有，何可兩立。

translations.literal: If the rat already has two existences, how can both stand?
translations.idiomatic: If the rat already has two existences, how can both stand?

sentences.zh: 光去此燭，得燃彼燭，神去此形，亦託彼形，又何惑哉？

translations.literal: Light leaves this candle and can ignite that candle; spirit leaves this form and also entrusts itself to that form — again, what confusion?"
translations.idiomatic: Light leaves this candle and can ignite that candle; spirit leaves this form and also entrusts itself to that form — again, what confusion?"

sentences.zh: 」邢云：「欲使土化為人，木生眼鼻，造化神明，不應如此。

translations.literal: " Xing said: "To want earth to transform into a human and wood to grow eyes and a nose — creation's spirit ought not to be like this."
translations.idiomatic: " Xing said, "To want earth to transform into a human and wood to grow eyes and a nose — creation's spirit ought not to be like this."

sentences.zh: 」弼曰：「腐草為螢，老木為蠍，造化不能，誰其然也？」

translations.literal: " Bi said: "Rotten grass becomes fireflies and old wood scorpions — creation cannot do it; who makes it so of itself?"
translations.idiomatic: " Bi said, "Rotten grass becomes fireflies and old wood scorpions — creation cannot do it; who makes it so of itself?"

sentences.zh: 其後別與邢書云：「夫建言明理，宜出典證，而違孔背釋，獨為君子。

translations.literal: Afterward he separately wrote Xing a letter saying: "In establishing words and clarifying principle, one ought to issue from canonical evidence; yet you turn your back on Confucius and Buddha and stand alone as a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he separately wrote Xing a letter saying, "In establishing words and clarifying principle, one ought to issue from canonical evidence; yet you turn your back on Confucius and Buddha and stand alone as a gentleman.

sentences.zh: 若不師聖，物各有心，馬首欲東，誰其能禦？

translations.literal: If one does not take the sages as teachers, each thing has its own heart — if the horse's head wants east, who can resist?
translations.idiomatic: If one does not take the sages as teachers, each thing has its own heart — if the horse's head wants east, who can resist?

sentences.zh: 奚取於適衷，何貴於得一。

translations.literal: What is taken from hitting the center, and what is valued in obtaining the one?
translations.idiomatic: What is taken from hitting the center, and what is valued in obtaining the one?

sentences.zh: 逸韻雖高，管見未喻。

translations.literal: Elegant rhyme though high, narrow view not understood."
translations.idiomatic: Elegant rhyme though high, narrow view not understood."

sentences.zh: 」前後往復再三，邢邵理屈而止，文多不載。

translations.literal: " Before and after, back and forth again and again three times; Xing Shao's principle was bent and he stopped — much of the text is not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: " Before and after, back and forth again and again three times; Xing Shao's argument gave way and he stopped — much of the text is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 又以本官行鄭州事，未發，為家客告弼謀反，收下獄，案治無實，久乃見原。

translations.literal: Again, while holding his original office he was assigned to administer Zhengzhou affairs; before he set out, a household retainer reported that Bi was plotting rebellion. He was arrested and imprisoned; the investigation found no substance, and only after a long time was he pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Again, while still in his original post, he was ordered to handle affairs at Zhengzhou. Before he set out, a household retainer accused him of plotting rebellion. He was arrested and jailed; the inquiry found nothing, and only after a long while was he forgiven.

sentences.zh: 因此絕朝見。

translations.literal: Because of this he ceased attending court.
translations.idiomatic: After that he stopped coming to court.

sentences.zh: 復坐第二子廷尉監臺卿斷獄稽遲，與寺官俱為郎中封靜哲所訟。

translations.literal: He was again punished because his second son Taiqing, as supervisory official of the Court of the Imperial Clan, was slow in handling cases, and he and the court officials were all sued by Langzhong Feng Jingzhe.
translations.idiomatic: He was punished again when his second son Taiqing, as supervisory official of the court of the imperial clan, was slow in deciding cases, and he and the court officials were all impeached by langzhong Feng Jingzhe.

sentences.zh: 事既上聞，顯祖發忿，遂徙弼臨海鎮。

translations.literal: When the matter reached the emperor's ears, Xianzu flew into a rage and transferred Bi to Linhai garrison.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter reached the throne, Gao Yang flew into a rage and transferred Bi to Linhai garrison.

sentences.zh: 時楚州人東方白額謀反，南北響應，臨海鎮為賊師張綽、潘天合等所攻，弼率厲城人，終得全固。

translations.literal: At that time Bai'e of Chuzhou plotted rebellion with north-south response; Linhai garrison was attacked by bandit leaders Zhang Chuo, Pan Tianhe, and others. Bi led and encouraged the townspeople and finally held the place secure.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Dongfang Bai'e of Chuzhou rose in rebellion with echoes north and south. Linhai garrison was attacked by bandit leaders Zhang Chuo, Pan Tianhe, and others. Bi rallied the townspeople and in the end held the place secure.

sentences.zh: 顯祖嘉之，勑行海州事，即所徙之州。

translations.literal: Xianzu praised this and ordered him to administer Haizhou affairs — the very province to which he had been transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang praised this and ordered him to administer Haizhou — the very province to which he had been sent.

sentences.zh: 在州奏通陵道並韓信故道。

translations.literal: In the province he memorialized concerning Tongling road and the old Han Xin road.
translations.idiomatic: In the province he memorialized on Tongling road and the old Han Xin road.

sentences.zh: 又於州東帶海而起長堰，外遏鹹潮，內引淡水。

translations.literal: Also east of the province by the sea he raised a long dike, blocking salt tide without and channeling fresh water within.
translations.idiomatic: East of the province along the coast he also raised a long dike, holding back the salt tide outside and drawing fresh water within.

sentences.zh: 勑並依行。

translations.literal: Edicts approved all and were carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts approved all of it and it was carried out.

sentences.zh: 轉徐州刺史，未之任，又除膠州刺史。

translations.literal: Transferred to inspector of Xuzhou; before taking office, he was again made inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to inspector of Xuzhou; before he took up the post he was again made inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 弼儒雅寬恕，尤曉史職。

translations.literal: Bi was refined and tolerant, especially expert in the duties of historiography.
translations.idiomatic: Bi was refined and forgiving, and above all skilled in the historian's craft.

sentences.zh: 所在清潔，為吏民所懷。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he was clean; officials and people cherished him.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he kept things clean, and officials and common people held him dear.

sentences.zh: 耽好玄理，老而愈篤。

translations.literal: He loved the profundities of mystery; in old age he grew ever more devoted.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the profundities of the dark learning; in old age he grew only more devoted.

sentences.zh: 又註《莊子•惠施篇》、《易上下繫》，名《新註義苑》，並行於世。

translations.literal: He also annotated the "Hui Shi" chapter of the Zhuangzi and the upper and lower appendices of the Changes, titled New Annotated Garden of Meanings, and both circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He also annotated the "Hui Shi" chapter of the Zhuangzi and the upper and lower appendices of the Changes, under the title New Annotated Garden of Meanings, and both circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 弼性質直，前在霸朝，多所匡正。

translations.literal: Bi's nature was upright; in the hegemonic court era he often corrected matters.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's nature was straight; in the hegemonic court he often set things right.

sentences.zh: 及顯祖作相，致位僚首，初聞揖讓之議，猶有諫言。

translations.literal: When Xianzu became chancellor and reached the head of the staff, on first hearing talk of yielding the throne he still offered remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yang became chancellor and rose to head the staff, on first hearing talk of yielding the throne he still spoke against it.

sentences.zh: 顯祖嘗問弼云：「治國當用何人？

translations.literal: Xianzu once asked Bi, "In governing a state, whom should one employ?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang once asked Bi, "In governing a state, whom should one employ?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「鮮卑車馬客，會須用中國人。

translations.literal: He replied, "For Xianbei chariot-and-horse guests, one still must use Chinese men."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "For Xianbei chariot-and-horse men, one still must use Chinese men."

sentences.zh: 」顯祖以為此言譏我。

translations.literal: Xianzu took this speech as mocking him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang took this as a jibe at himself.

sentences.zh: 高德政居要，不能下之，乃於衆前面折云：「黃門在帝左右，何得聞善不驚，唯好減削抑挫！

translations.literal: Gao Dezheng held a key post and could not put up with him; before the crowd he openly rebuked him, saying, "Yellow Gate attendants are at the emperor's side — how can they hear what is good and not be startled, and only love to cut, trim, and suppress!"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Dezheng held a key post and could not bring himself below Bi; before the assembly he openly rebuked him: "Yellow Gate men stand at the emperor's side — how can they hear what is good and not be stirred, and only love to pare away and crush?"

sentences.zh: 」德政深以為恨，數言其短。

translations.literal: Dezheng bore deep resentment and many times spoke of his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Dezheng nursed deep hatred and spoke of his faults again and again.

sentences.zh: 又令主書杜永珍密啟弼在長史日，受人請屬，大營婚嫁。

translations.literal: He also had chief secretary Du Yongzhen secretly report that during Bi's days as chief clerk he accepted entreaties and on a great scale arranged marriage festivities.
translations.idiomatic: He also had chief secretary Du Yongzhen secretly report that in Bi's days as chief clerk he took bribes and on a great scale staged marriage festivities.

sentences.zh: 顯祖內銜之。

translations.literal: Xianzu harbored it inwardly.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang nursed it inwardly.

sentences.zh: 弼恃舊，仍有公事陳請。

translations.literal: Bi, relying on old ties, still made official requests on public business.
translations.idiomatic: Bi, trusting in old ties, still pressed official requests.

sentences.zh: 十年夏，上因飲酒，積其愆失，遂遣就州斬之，時年六十九。

translations.literal: In the summer of the tenth year, the emperor, while drinking, accumulated his faults and sent orders to execute him at the province; he was sixty-nine at the time.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the tenth year the emperor, while drinking, piled up his faults and sent orders to execute him in his province; he was sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 既而悔之，驛追不及。

translations.literal: Soon he regretted it and sent couriers in pursuit, but they could not overtake.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he regretted it and sent couriers in pursuit, but they could not catch up.

sentences.zh: 長子蕤、第四子光，遠徙臨海鎮。

translations.literal: His eldest son Rui and fourth son Guang were exiled far to Linhai garrison.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Rui and fourth son Guang were exiled far to Linhai garrison.

sentences.zh: 次子臺卿，先徙東豫州。

translations.literal: His second son Taiqing had already been exiled to Eastern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Taiqing had already been exiled to Eastern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 幹明初，並得還鄴。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Ganming they were all allowed to return to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Ganming they were all allowed to return to Ye.

sentences.zh: 天統五年，追贈弼使持節、揚郢二州軍事、開府儀同三司、尚書右僕射、揚州刺史，諡曰文肅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tiantong he was posthumously enfeoffed with Bi as Bearer of the Staff, military commander of Yang and E provinces, Grand Master Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and inspector of Yang Province, with posthumous title Wen Su.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tiantong, Bi was posthumously given bearer of the staff, command of Yang and E provinces, grand master equal in rank to the three dukes, right vice director of the masters of writing, and inspector of Yang Province, with posthumous title Wen Su.

sentences.zh: 蕤、臺卿，並有學業。

translations.literal: Rui and Taiqing both had learning.
translations.idiomatic: Rui and Taiqing both had learning.

sentences.zh: 臺卿文筆尤工，見稱當世。

translations.literal: Taiqing's literary brush was especially skilled and he was praised in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Taiqing's brush was especially fine, and his own age praised him.

sentences.zh: 蕤字子美，武平中大理少卿，兼散騎常侍，聘陳使主。

translations.literal: Rui, styled Zimei, in Wuping was vice director of the Court of Judicature and concurrent regular attendant, and chief of the mission to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, styled Zimei, in Wuping was vice director of the court of judicature and concurrent regular attendant, and headed the mission to Chen.

sentences.zh: 末年，吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In his later years he was a langzhong in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he was a langzhong in the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，終於開州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Sui Kaihuang he ended his days as inspector of Kai Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui Kaihuang he ended his days as inspector of Kai Province.

sentences.zh: 臺卿字少山，歷中書、黃門侍郎，兼大著作、修國史。

translations.literal: Taiqing, styled Shaoshan, served in succession as secretariat and Yellow Gate vice director, and concurrently as grand author and compiler of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Taiqing, styled Shaoshan, served in turn as secretariat and Yellow Gate vice director, and concurrently as grand author and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 武平末，國子祭酒，領尚書左丞。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuping he was libationer of the Imperial University and concurrently held the post of left vice director in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was libationer of the imperial university and concurrently left vice director in the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，命尚書左僕射陽休之以下知名朝士十八人隨駕入關，蕤兄弟並不預此名。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he ordered eighteen noted court scholars from Yang Xiuzhi, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, downward to follow the imperial train into Guan; the Rui brothers were not among those named.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he ordered eighteen noted court scholars from Yang Xiuzhi, left vice director of the masters of writing, downward to follow the train into Guan; the Rui brothers were not on the list.

sentences.zh: 臺卿後雖被徵，為其聾疾放歸。

translations.literal: Taiqing was later summoned, but because of deafness he was released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Taiqing was later summoned, but because of deafness he was released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，徵為著作郎，歲餘以年老致事，詔許之。

translations.literal: Under Sui Kaihuang he was summoned as author in the Masters of Writing; after a little more than a year, on account of age he retired from office, and an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui Kaihuang he was summoned as author in the masters of writing; after a little more than a year, on account of age he retired, and an edict allowed it.

sentences.zh: 特優其禮，終身給祿，未幾而終。

translations.literal: His rites were especially favored; salary was granted for life, and before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: His rites were especially favored; salary was granted for life, and before long he died.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：孫搴便藩左右，處文墨之地，入幕未久，情義已深。

translations.literal: The historian writes: Sun Qian was at the prince's convenient side in a place of brush and ink; he had entered the staff not long, yet bonds were already deep.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Sun Qian stood at the prince's side in the place of brush and ink; he had entered the staff not long, yet affection was already deep.

sentences.zh: 及倉卒致殞，高祖折我右臂，雖戎旌未卷，愛惜才子，不然何以成霸王之業。

translations.literal: When he suddenly died, the Grand Ancestor said he had broken his right arm — though military banners had not yet been rolled up, he cherished talented men; otherwise how could one achieve hegemonic enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: When he suddenly died, Gao Huan said he had broken his right arm — though the banners of war had not yet been furled, he cherished men of talent; otherwise how could one achieve a hegemon's work.

sentences.zh: 太史公云：「非死者難，處死者難。

translations.literal: The Grand Historian said: "It is not dying that is hard; it is facing death that is hard."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian said: "It is not dying that is hard; it is facing death that is hard."

sentences.zh: 」「或重於太山，或輕於鴻毛。

translations.literal: "Some weigh heavier than Mount Tai; some are lighter than a goose feather."
translations.idiomatic: "Some weigh heavier than Mount Tai; some are lighter than a goose feather."

sentences.zh: 」斯其義也。

translations.literal: This is the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the meaning.

sentences.zh: 元康以智能才幹，委質霸朝，綢繆帷幄，任寄為重。

translations.literal: Yuankang, with intelligence and talent, entrusted himself to the hegemonic court, intimate in the tent, with weighty trust.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang, with intelligence and talent, gave himself to the hegemonic court, intimate in the command tent, with weighty trust.

sentences.zh: 及難無茍免，忘生殉義，可謂得其地焉。

translations.literal: At the difficulty he did not seek escape; he forgot life and followed righteousness — one may say he found his place.
translations.idiomatic: At the crisis he did not seek escape; he forgot life and followed righteousness — one may say he met his place.

sentences.zh: 楊愔自謂異行奇才，冠絕夷等，弒逆之際，趨而避之，是則非處死者難，死者亦難也。

translations.literal: Yang Yin considered himself of unusual conduct and peerless talent above the barbarian ranks; at the time of regicide he rushed to flee — so it is not that facing death is hard; dying is also hard.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin thought himself of unusual conduct and talent above the barbarian ranks; at the regicide he rushed to flee — so it is not that facing death is hard; dying is hard too.

sentences.zh: 顯祖弱齡藏器，未有朝臣所知，及北宮之難，以年次推重，故受終之議，時未之許焉。

translations.literal: Xianzu in youth concealed his talent; no court minister knew him. At the crisis of the Northern Palace, by order of age he was pressed forward — therefore the succession was not yet accepted at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang in youth concealed his gifts; no court minister knew him. At the crisis of the Northern Palace, by order of age he was pressed forward — so the succession was not yet accepted at the time.

sentences.zh: 杜弼識學甄明，發言讜正，禪代之際，先起異圖。

translations.literal: Du Bi's learning was discerning and clear; his speech was upright counsel. At the abdication transition he first raised dissenting views.
translations.idiomatic: Du Bi's learning was discerning and clear; his speech was upright counsel. At the abdication he was first to raise a different plan.

sentences.zh: 王怒未怠息，卒蒙顯戮。

translations.literal: The king's anger had not yet subsided when he at last suffered manifest execution.
translations.idiomatic: The king's anger had not yet cooled when he at last suffered open execution.

sentences.zh: 直言多矣，能無及是者乎？

translations.literal: Straight words were many — could one avoid reaching this?
translations.idiomatic: Straight words were many — who could avoid coming to this?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：彥舉驅馳，才高行诐。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Yanjun galloping — talent high, conduct crooked.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Yanjun galloping — talent high, conduct crooked.

sentences.zh: 元康忠勇，舍生存義。

translations.literal: Yuankang loyal and brave — he gave up life and kept righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang loyal and brave — he gave up life and kept righteousness.

sentences.zh: 卬卬輔玄，思極談天，道亡時晦，身沒名全。

translations.literal: Lofty Fuxuan — thought reached talk of heaven; the Way perished, the times dark; body destroyed, name whole.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty Fuxuan — thought reached talk of heaven; the Way was lost, the times dark; body destroyed, name whole.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
translations.idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
